item.title: France Macron dit vouloir punir les "casseurs" et écouter les manifestants
item.description: Emmanuel Macron a fait dimanche la distinction entre les "casseurs" et les manifestants aux "revendications légitimes", invitant le gouvernement à faire en sorte que le chaos constaté la veille "ne puisse pas se reproduire".
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Emmanuel Macron a fait dimanche la distinction entre les "casseurs" et les manifestants aux "revendications légitimes", invitant le gouvernement à faire en sorte que le chaos constaté la veille "ne puisse pas se reproduire". "Notre responsabilité est double : entendre la colère et agir sur ses causes, et faire respecter fermement l'ordre républicain. Nous ne devons ni confondre les revendications légitimes avec la violence, ni laisser les violences empêcher que ces revendications soient entendues", a dit le président lors d'une allocution à l'Elysée. Le chef de l'Etat a réuni dimanche après-midi le Premier ministre, Sébastien Lecornu, et les ministres concernés par les manifestations de la veille qui ont été émaillées d'affrontements, de destructions de bâtiments publics et de pillages dans tout le pays. Plusieurs centaines de policiers ont été blessés et près de 2.400 individus ont été interpellés, selon le ministère de l'Intérieur. "Des factieux issus de groupuscules d'ultra-gauche rejoints par de nombreux délinquants se sont livrés à une violence débridées dans nos villes", a dit Emmanuel Macron. "Rien de le justifie, rien de l'explique, rien ne l'excuse", a-t-il poursuivi, annonçant pour ce lundi une "cellule de crise" présidée par Sébastien Lecornu "pour mobiliser les aides les plus rapides". Les maires de Paris, Lyon et Marseille et une partie de l'opposition ont critiqué la gestion du maintien de l'ordre par l'exécutif. "Nos forces de l'ordre, malgré leur professionnalisme ont eu à subir une violence inouïe", a dit Emmanuel Macron. "J'ai demandé au gouvernement d'en tirer toutes les leçons en terme de renseignement et d'anticipation et faire en sorte que cela ne puisse pas se reproduire. J'attends des réponses claires et toute la transparence sera faite." "CEUX QUI ONT DÉTRUIT DOIVENT PAYER" Pour prévenir tout nouveau débordement, Emmanuel Macron a demandé aux préfets de prendre des décisions "en lien avec les maires" allant "jusqu'à interdire certains rassemblements". Il a aussi appelé "l'ensemble des partis politiques, des organisations professionnelles et syndicales", prochainement réunis par le Premier ministre, "à condamner sans ambiguïté toutes les violences et à appeler au calme". "Le pays a besoin d'ordre, d'apaisement et pas d'une escalade", a-t-il considéré à six mois d'une élection présidentielle pour laquelle "nous avons besoin d'unité de calme et de respect". Emmanuel Macron s'est adressé sans la nommer à La France insoumise de Jean-Luc Mélenchon, accusée par le Premier ministre et une partie de la classe politique d'encourager les manifestations violentes. "Tous ceux qui vous expliquent que l'urgence est de manifester et d'aller dans la rue n'ont qu'un but : abîmer la République et voler le débat", a dit Emmanuel Macron. Pour ce qui est des responsables des violences, "ceux qui ont détruit doivent payer, ceux qui ont pillé doivent rembourser, ceux qui ont cherché à faire tomber la République auront à en répondre" a dit le président. Emmanuel Macron s'est aussi adressé aux manifestants qui ont défilé par centaines de milliers samedi contre la vie chère et la situation dans les lycées et les universités, notamment. "Jamais nous ne devons confondre ces derniers avec ceux qui ont détruit, cassé, pillé", a-t-il dit. Evoquant les jeunes qui manifestent depuis des semaines, le président a estimé que "leur parole doit être entendue, sans a priori et sans minimiser les difficultés". Emmanuel Macron doit effectuer en début de semaine une tournée au Proche-Orient qui le conduira au Koweït, aux Emirats arabes unis, à Bahreïn et au Qatar. Le chef de l'Etat n'a pas changé son programme malgré la situation en France, a fait savoir son entourage.

item.title: McLaren vai vender cinco carros de F1, todos pilotados por campeões e um por Brad Pitt
item.description: A McLaren está vendendo cinco carros de Fórmula 1 em pleno funcionamento, pilotados por campeões, incluindo Lewis Hamilton e o falecido Ayrton Senna, sendo que um deles também foi testado pelo ator de Hollywood Brad Pitt.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: A McLaren está vendendo cinco carros de Fórmula 1 em pleno funcionamento, pilotados por campeões, incluindo Lewis Hamilton e o falecido Ayrton Senna, sendo que um deles também foi testado pelo ator de Hollywood Brad Pitt. Os carros, que serão vendidos por meio do revendedor de luxo Tom Hartley Jr. e devem arrecadar dezenas de milhões de dólares, serão preparados pela atual campeã do campeonato de construtores para seus próximos proprietários. Hartley Jr. também vendeu a coleção do [USN:L3N3PQ0Q7 TEXT:"ex-chefe da F1 Bernie Ecclestone"] e 20 carros de passeio que pertenciam ao falecido coproprietário da McLaren, [USN:L4N3UJ12T TEXT:"Mansour Ojjeh."] “Decidimos nos desfazer desses icônicos carros de Fórmula 1 da McLaren porque achamos que mantê-los simplesmente guardados em um depósito é um desserviço ao que eles representam”, disse o presidente-executivo da McLaren Racing, Zak Brown, em comunicado divulgado neste domingo. “Esses carros foram construídos para serem dirigidos e competir, e queremos vê-los sendo usados e apreciados. Acreditamos que essa seja a melhor maneira de manter viva nossa história e ativo nosso negócio de patrimônio.” PITT DIRIGIU UM DELES APÓS FILMAGENS DE FILME Os cinco carros abrangem 32 anos da história da McLaren, começando com dois carros MP4/6A (chassis números 04 e 07 com motores Honda V12) pilotados pelo austríaco Gerhard Berger e testados por Senna durante a campanha que resultou no título de 1991. O chassi 04 ficou em segundo lugar em uma dobradinha no Grande Prêmio de San Marino, com as McLaren dando voltas à frente de todo o pelotão. O chassi 07 ficou em segundo lugar no Grande Prêmio da Inglaterra, corrida realizada em casa para a McLaren. Ambos estão na posse da McLaren desde então. Um McLaren MP4/27A de 2012 (chassi 01), pilotado pelo campeão mundial de 2009, Jenson Button, e testado pelo heptacampeão mundial Hamilton, também está à venda. Dois carros pilotados exclusivamente pelo atual campeão Lando Norris em 2021 e 2023 completam o lote. O McLaren MCL35M de 2021 levou Norris ao pódio em Ímola, Mônaco e Monza, enquanto o MCL37A-03 de 2023 venceu corridas consecutivas em Cingapura e no Japão e foi testado após o fim da temporada por um grupo de pilotos, incluindo o companheiro de equipe de Norris, Oscar Piastri, e Mick Schumacher, filho do grande Michael da F1. O McLaren de 2023 foi pilotado por Pitt em um teste privado no Circuito das Américas, em Austin, em junho do ano passado, em conexão com seu papel de protagonista no filme “F1: O Filme”, e é o carro de F1 mais moderno oferecido à venda para um proprietário particular. Pitt teria atingido uma velocidade de 197 mph (317 km/h) com o carro. “É extremamente raro que um colecionador tenha a oportunidade de adquirir carros de Grande Prêmio que participaram de corridas diretamente do fabricante e da equipe que os construíram e competiram com eles, e isso torna esta uma oferta muito especial”, disse Hartley. “Esses cinco carros serão oferecidos individualmente e não há qualquer pressão de tempo. Nossa prioridade, e a da McLaren, é encontrar os donos certos para eles.” Embora nenhum preço tenha sido divulgado, espera-se que os valores variem de 5 milhões de libras (US$6,7 milhões) a até 10 milhões. Um McLaren MP4-25A pilotado por Hamilton na vitória na Turquia em 2010 foi vendido por 4,8 milhões de libras em 2021, enquanto uma Ferrari vencedora de 2001, pilotada por Michael Schumacher, alcançou US$ 7,5 milhões em Nova York em 2017. (Reportagem de Alan Baldwin)

item.title: Milan protests turn violent as demonstrators clash with police over rising living costs
item.description: The unrest came a day after similar demonstrations and clashes were reported in several Italian cities, highlighting growing public discontent over the cost of living and the quality of public services
item.dc:creator: Livemint
item.content:encoded: Police clashed with protesters in Milan on Sunday as demonstrations over rising living costs and poor public services turned violent, with demonstrators throwing stones, breaking shop windows and setting rubbish bins on fire. Riot police used tear gas and water cannons to disperse several hundred hooded protesters near the central Piazza Duomo, according to Reuters, citing sources. More than 60 protesters were taken to police stations for further checks, the report said. The unrest came a day after similar demonstrations and clashes were reported in several Italian cities, highlighting growing public discontent over the cost of living and the quality of public services. The latest violence added to pressure on Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government, which is preparing to address the situation at a meeting scheduled for Monday. 28 protesters arrested after Saturday clashes Italian police arrested 28 protesters following clashes on Saturday in several northern cities, including Milan, Bologna, Brescia, Bergamo and Turin, according to a police report released on Sunday. The demonstrations spread across urban centres as protesters voiced concerns over rising household expenses and public services. Authorities faced the challenge of containing the unrest while restoring order in areas affected by vandalism and clashes. In Milan, the use of tear gas and water cannons followed incidents involving protesters who broke shop windows and set fire to bins near one of the city's central landmarks. The latest incidents came amid a broader wave of demonstrations across parts of Europe, where rising living costs and concerns about public services have fuelled public anger. Unrest draws comparisons with protests in France The violence in Italy echoed unrest in neighbouring France, where hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets on Saturday over rising costs and declining public services. The demonstrations in France were among the country's most violent in years, according to the report. The developments have drawn attention to mounting economic and social pressures facing governments across Europe, particularly as households contend with higher expenses and growing concerns about the quality and accessibility of public services. Although the demonstrations took place in different countries, the grievances cited in both cases included the cost of living and dissatisfaction with public services. The scale of the protests has also raised questions about how governments will respond to public demands while maintaining law and order. Meloni calls government meeting to address situation Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni condemned the violence and announced that her government would meet on Monday to discuss how to respond to the situation. Meloni faces an election next year, adding political significance to the government's handling of the demonstrations. The planned meeting is expected to focus on the situation following the clashes, although specific measures to address the protesters' grievances were not detailed in the report. The government faces the twin challenges of responding to concerns about living costs and public services while preventing further violence and damage to businesses. The latest clashes underscore the pressure on European governments to address economic concerns that have increasingly featured in public demonstrations. Further developments will depend on the government's response and whether authorities can contain the unrest while addressing the issues raised by demonstrators.

item.title: Anthropic to commit 5% stake to new 'public benefit fund'
item.description: AI lab Anthropic, the developer of Claude, said on Sunday it will commit 5% of its shares to a new public benefit fund so it has increased flexibility and scale to make donations for the "public good."
item.dc:creator: Abu Sultan
item.content:encoded: AI lab Anthropic, the developer of Claude, said on Sunday it will commit 5% of its shares to a new public benefit fund so it has increased flexibility and scale to make donations for the "public good." The proposed fund would be established as a wholly owned limited liability company and would receive an additional 2% of Anthropic's shares, at the board's discretion, for every 50% increase in the company's value above a baseline that has yet to be disclosed. The move comes at a time when Anthropic is planning one of the biggest IPOs in history as a [USN:L6N45L0UH TEXT:"public benefit corporation"], a legal structure that requires management to consider certain broader interests as well as turning a profit for investors. The company, which has positioned itself as a safety-first AI lab, has said AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity" and devoted roughly 80 pages of the 261-page main body of its prospectus to laying out risk factors. Anthropic said in its blog post its Public Benefit Fund could support initiatives including nonprofit donations, direct distributions to specific populations and efforts to address AI’s impact on the labor market. Elon Musk, who runs Anthropic rival xAI, on X said he recommended "giving the shares directly to the public." Anthropic cited the potential impact of AI on workers as one area of focus for the new fund, building on a previously announced $200 million commitment to study and address labor-market disruption. Global companies have [USN:L6N42P0Q1 TEXT:"cut"] thousands of jobs after investing heavily in AI, with many, primarily tech firms, pointing to higher efficiencies from the technology's rapid adoption. IMF research [USN:L1N45Z05I TEXT:"shows"] that some 40% of jobs will be either augmented, downgraded or eliminated by AI, with the number as high as 60% in advanced economies, Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said last week. NOT FOR POLITICAL GIVING The AI giant said none of the equity held by its fund would be used for lobbying or political giving in the United States or abroad. US [USN:L6N43N198 TEXT:"policymakers"] are weighing greater oversight of artificial intelligence and AI companies are stepping up efforts to shape how the technology is regulated. Combined with its co-founders' pledge to donate 80% of their equity and an employee donation matching program, roughly 20% of Anthropic's shares will be dedicated to public purposes, excluding any additional shares added later. Anthropic said it would say more in the coming months on the fund's governance, structure and the valuation thresholds that could expand its ownership stake. It also plans to publish a public-benefit report detailing progress toward its mission.

Four killed after high winds turn grass fire deadly at Canadian military base, report says

The base, one of Canada's largest, is about 210 km east of Edmonton in Alberta.

CALGARY: A fire at an Alberta military base that killed at least four people and seriously injured dozens started with a smouldering grass fire that was whipped into a wall of flames by high winds, Canada's Globe and Mail newspaper reported on Sunday (Oct 18). The fire then engulfed Canadian Armed Forces members at a firing range, the newspaper said, citing internal military communications. The Canadian government on Sunday confirmed four deaths at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright but has not publicly commented on the cause of the fire, which took place at about 4pm on Saturday (6am Sunday, Singapore time) in a training area at the base as winds gusted up to 96kmh. Prime Minister Mark Carney said the fire was one of the worst peacetime tragedies ever for Canada's armed forces on home soil.

"The nation is in mourning for those brave members of our Armed Forces whom we have lost," Carney said Sunday, adding that he had ordered flags on federal buildings across the country to be lowered to half-staff to honour the victims. CBC, the government-funded national broadcaster, previously reported seven deaths at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, citing unnamed sources. Canadian authorities have said the situation continues to evolve, and that they will not confirm casualty figures until next of kin have been notified. Internal military communications indicate that the fire "very seriously" injured 31 people, the Globe and Mail reported. CFB Wainwright had 1,310 military and civilian personnel stationed there as of 2021, according to census data.  The base, one of Canada's largest, is about 210 km east of Edmonton in Alberta. National Defence Minister David McGuinty said on Sunday he would go to the city for briefings on the situation. The base houses the Canadian Manoeuvre Training Centre, which runs training scenarios and exercises for the army. Carney said those affected in Saturday's fire came from military bases across the country.

People attend a church service, the day after a serious incident that resulted in a fire caused deaths and injuries at Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Wainwright, in Wainwright, Alberta, Canada, Oct 18, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Jennifer Gauthier)

Military and civilian firefighters fought the fire through the night in "some of the worst conditions imaginable", Carney said. Canadian officials are expected to address the public from Wainwright, which is located in a largely rural area, later on Sunday afternoon. Air ambulances from Edmonton and Saskatoon, which is about 300 km from Wainwright, flew to the military base on Saturday, Carney said. Patients are being treated in Edmonton, Wainwright, Calgary and Red Deer, he said. Health staff in Edmonton said a "code orange", or mass-casualty event, was declared to coordinate the medical response for patients being transported from Wainwright, CBC News reported. The town of Wainwright, with a population of about 6,600, is just north of the base. The municipality posted on social media that the fire had crossed the base fence into the nearby district but no evacuation orders had been issued. It said on Sunday that the fire is not expected to spread beyond its current boundaries.

Source: Reuters/fs

item.title: Wake Forest baseball coach Tom Walter placed on leave
item.description: Wake Forest has placed longtime baseball coach Tom Walter on leave, the university confirmed.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Wake Forest has placed longtime baseball coach Tom Walter on leave, the university confirmed. The school issued a statement Saturday after Wake Forest-centered site Demon Deacons Digest reported the news. No reason for the move has been disclosed. "Wake Forest baseball head coach Tom Walter is on leave effective October 14, 2026," spokesperson Ryan Madden told the outlet. "Additional information will be shared when it becomes appropriate. In accordance with University policy Wake Forest Athletics will have no further comment at this time." Eric Niesen, an assistant coach on the pitching side, currently is in charge of the program, with an assist from administrator Craig Zakrzewski. Before returning to his alma mater as a coach before the 2026 season, Niesen served as director of pitching for the Houston Astros. Walter began as the Demon Deacons' head coach in June 2009. The program made a fifth consecutive appearance in the NCAA Tournament in 2026 and reached the Men's College World Series in 2023. Chase Burns, Nick Kurtz, Gavin Sheets and Rhett Lowder are among the current major leaguers to have played for Walter. Walter was in the news in June 2025 after he appeared to utter a homophobic slur as his team lost to Tennessee in the NCAA Knoxville Regional. Video of the incident spread, and Walter apologized the next day. Athletic director John Currie called the conduct "disappointing" in a public rebuke. Walter has 536 career wins at Wake Forest. He owns a career record of 964-738-1 that includes his years as head coach at George Washington (1997-2004) and New Orleans (2005-09). He became the seventh coach to lead three programs to the NCAA Tournament at the Division I level. --Field Level Media

item.title: Report: Saints QB Tyler Shough playing with broken bones in left hand
item.description: New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough will once again be under center on Sunday against the New York Giants while playing with multiple broken bones in his non-throwing hand, ESPN reported.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough will once again be under center on Sunday against the New York Giants while playing with multiple broken bones in his non-throwing hand, ESPN reported. The Saints have listed Shough on the injury report with a hand injury, but the specifics have not been revealed by the team. He has continued to play through the injury that reportedly occurred in the Saints' 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons on Oct. 5. Shough has played with his ring and pinky fingers taped together while wearing a protective glove. It has not impacted his ability to pass the ball and he has completed handoffs on running plays with his right throwing hand. The injury is expected to take multiple months to fully heal, according to the report, with New Orleans set to go on its bye week after playing the Pittsburgh Steelers next Sunday in Paris. Shough, 27, has completed 66.8% of his passes for 1,299 yards and nine touchdowns with five interceptions as the Saints carried a 1-4 record into Sunday's game against the Giants. In two NFL seasons, the Saints' 2025 second-round draft pick has completed 67.3% of his passes for 3,683 yards, 19 touchdowns and 11 interceptions in 16 games, while New Orleans has gone 6-8 in his 14 starts. --Field Level Media

item.title: Brighton's patience pays off as Huerzeler helps Seagulls soar
item.description: Eight months after some Brighton & Hove Albion fans called for Fabian Huerzeler to be sacked after a home defeat by Crystal Palace, the young manager has the Seagulls soaring in third place in the Premier League after Sunday's 5-0 rout of the same opponents.
item.dc:creator: Rohith Nair
item.content:encoded: Eight months after some Brighton & Hove Albion fans called for Fabian Huerzeler to be sacked after a home defeat by Crystal Palace, the young manager has the Seagulls soaring in third place in the Premier League after Sunday's 5-0 rout of the same opponents. The 33-year-old, the youngest manager in the English top flight, watched his side demolish rivals Palace in a game capped by [USN:L4N464024 TEXT:"Diego Gomez's spectacular halfway-line strike"] that sent the home fans into raptures. It was a far cry from February's 1-0 defeat in the "M23 Derby" that left Brighton languishing in 14th place as some of the club's fans chanted "You're getting sacked in the morning." Brighton, however, refused to push the panic button and retained their faith in Huerzeler, who eventually guided the south-coast club to an eighth-placed finish. Chairman Tony Bloom [USN:L1N41K15A TEXT:"rewarded Huerzeler with a contract extension"] until 2029 and the club are reaping the benefits of the trust placed in the young German. LEAGUE-LEADING 23 GOALS With Sunday's 5-0 victory, Brighton sit five points behind leaders Manchester City with a league-leading 23 goals in seven games, five clean sheets and a goal difference of plus 18, six better than City's. "A few months ago (after losing to Palace) we were in a different place and I said I'd keep pushing to get another opportunity to beat them, so I'm happy we did it today," Huerzeler told Sky Sports. "It's not a one-man show, so I credit my players and my staff. Hopefully everyone enjoyed it." While Erling Haaland has scored eight of City's goals to move clear in the Golden Boot race, Brighton have already had 11 different scorers. "If you look, they're shared around a lot which is a massive help. We've got everyone chipping in and helping out the team," Brighton defender Lewis Dunk told BBC Radio. "If you look at our clean sheets, I think it's the most we've ever had at this part of the season, so we're buzzing with that as well." RELENTLESS PRESSING Brighton's success in the new campaign has been built on relentless pressing, a hallmark of last month's commanding 3-0 victory over champions Arsenal that left coach [USN:L6N45B053 TEXT:"Mikel Arteta searching for answers"] after his side's first defeat of the season. Pascal Gross's successful return has provided another major boost. The 35-year-old, who previously spent seven seasons at Brighton, rejoined the club earlier this year in search of regular first-team football. Gross is their joint-top scorer with three goals while the German also leads the team with four assists. It was his free kick that forced an own goal in the fourth minute that opened the floodgates against Palace. Dunk refused to entertain talk of a title challenge so early in the season, while Huerzeler was equally determined to keep expectations in check. "To me, the most important thing is the things we can improve... It's good to celebrate the win, but understand there is still space for improvement, especially for individual players," he said. "We have to keep going. We can't be satisfied. We have to keep pushing, stay humble and understand why we are successful at the moment to keep pushing at that level."

item.title: Trump endorses Netanyahu's re-election bid after months of strained ties
item.description: Trump backed Netanyahu nine days before Israel's October 27 election, while rival Gadi Eisenkot said only Israeli citizens would decide who becomes the next prime minister ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By María Paula Mijares Torres US President Donald Trump endorsed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu following months of increasing strain between the two leaders. Trump’s endorsement marks a late intervention in Israel’s election, reversing months of public hesitation and renewed tensions with Netanyahu just nine days before the October 27 election, the first since Hamas attacked Israel on October 7, 2023, killing 1,200 Israelis and injuring and capturing hundreds more. “Bibi Netanyahu has been Strong, Brave, and Brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself,” Trump wrote in a social media post on Sunday. “Please let this Letter serve to represent my Complete and Total Endorsement of Bibi Netanyahu in his upcoming Race for Re-Election as Prime Minister of Israel.” Netanyahu is in a close race to keep his leadership position as tensions from the Iran war and the conflicts in Gaza and the West Bank test his popularity. At the same time, Trump is also less popular in Israel than at the beginning of the Iran war in February. The prime minister’s top election rival, Gadi Eisenkot, thanked Trump for being an Israeli ally, but added in an interview on Israeli Channel 12 on Sunday that the election is an internal matter. “Only the citizens of Israel will decide who will be the next prime minister,” he said. It used to be rare for US presidents to publicly weigh in on foreign elections, but Trump has sought to make his mark on behalf of his favoured leaders or candidates around the world. The two leaders’ once-tight bond has loosened over Netanyahu’s failure to toe Trump’s line on Gaza, Lebanon and the Iran war. As recently as Thursday, Trump stopped short of an endorsement and said he didn’t “trust anybody” in politics. In an interview with Time magazine earlier this month, Trump sidestepped multiple questions about Netanyahu’s re-election bid. On Tuesday, Trump told reporters on the White House lawn, “We haven’t even thought about it.

item.title: Trump says Washington golf course renovation to start in November, despite judge's order
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that his administration would begin renovation work next month on a historic Washington golf course that a federal judge had ordered could not proceed without prior court notification.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that his administration would begin renovation work next month on a historic Washington golf course that a federal judge had ordered could not proceed without prior court notification. The renovation work, which Trump earlier this year had said [USN:L1N43005N TEXT:"would begin in September"], has become the subject of a lawsuit over environmental and historic preservation concerns. Trump said in a post on Truth Social that work on the East Potomac Golf Links would begin on November 15 and that it would reopen in about 15 months. The renovation is among [USN:L6N41H110 TEXT:"a number of projects"] Trump is pursuing to reshape the White House and other Washington landmarks. US District Judge Ana Reyes ruled earlier this year that the government must give notice before any substantive construction work on the golf course could proceed, and last week [USN:L1N45Y0L4 TEXT:"issued an order"] halting the removal of trees at the site, which she called "inexcusable." The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment on whether Trump's announcement on Sunday would conflict with Reyes' directives. The DC Preservation League brought a lawsuit in February to halt the administration's takeover of the golf course, alleging that it would violate environmental laws and "irreparably destroy a priceless piece of American history." In an October 9 court filing, the Trump administration had asked Reyes to dismiss the litigation, saying it was premature because the "proposed project remains at an early and conceptual stage." The following day, however, the government removed about 500 trees from the site, which it said would improve safety at the park and restore its original design, and was part of a 2019 plan that predates Trump's ambitions for the course. Reyes ordered a halt to the removals. On Friday, the government filed a motion to disqualify Reyes and move the case to another district judge, saying her actions had shown "deep-seated and unequivocal antipathy toward the Trump Administration," according to court records.

item.title: McLaren to sell five F1 cars, all driven by champions and one by Brad Pitt
item.description: McLaren are selling five fully-functioning Formula One cars driven by champions, including Lewis Hamilton and the late Brazilian Ayrton Senna, with one also tested by Hollywood actor Brad Pitt.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: McLaren are selling five fully-functioning Formula One cars driven by champions, including Lewis Hamilton and the late Brazilian Ayrton Senna, with one also tested by Hollywood actor Brad Pitt. The cars, to be sold through high-end dealer Tom Hartley Jr. and expected to raise tens of millions of dollars, will be prepared by the reigning constructors' champions for their next owners. Hartley Jr. also sold the collection of [USN:L3N3PQ0Q7 TEXT:"former F1 supremo Bernie Ecclestone"] and 20 road cars belonging to the late McLaren co-owner [USN:L4N3UJ12T TEXT:"Mansour Ojjeh."] "We have decided to part with these iconic McLaren Formula One cars because we feel that having them simply sitting in storage is a disservice to what they represent," McLaren Racing CEO Zak Brown said in a statement on Sunday. "These cars were built to be driven and raced, and we want to see them being used and enjoyed. We believe that is the best way to keep our history alive and our heritage business active." PITT DROVE ONE AFTER FILMING F1 MOVIE The five span 32 years of McLaren history, starting with two MP4/6A cars (chassis numbers 04 and 07 with Honda V12 engines) raced by Austrian Gerhard Berger and tested by Senna during the 1991 title-winning campaign. Chassis 04 finished second in a one-two at the San Marino Grand Prix with the McLarens lapping the entire field. Chassis 07 came second at McLaren's home British Grand Prix. Both have been in McLaren's possession ever since. A 2012 McLaren MP4/27A (chassis 01) raced by 2009 world champion Jenson Button and tested by seven-times world champion Hamilton is also for sale. Two cars raced exclusively by reigning champion Lando Norris in 2021 and 2023 complete the group. The 2021 McLaren MCL35M took Norris to the podium in Imola, Monaco and Monza while the 2023 MCL37A-03 won successive races in Singapore and Japan and was tested post-season by a roster of drivers including Norris's teammate Oscar Piastri and Mick Schumacher, son of F1 great Michael. The 2023 McLaren was driven by Pitt in a private test at Austin's Circuit of the Americas in June last year in connection with his starring role in "F1 the Movie" and is the most modern F1 car offered for sale to a private owner. Pitt reportedly took it up to a speed of 197mph (317kph). "It is incredibly rare for a collector to have the opportunity to acquire race-driven Grand Prix cars directly from the manufacturer and team that built and campaigned them, and that makes this a very special offering," said Hartley. "These five cars will be offered individually and there is no time pressure whatsoever. Our priority, and McLaren’s, is to find the right homes for them." Although no prices were given, they are expected to range from 5 million pounds ($6.7 million) to as much as 10 million. A McLaren MP4-25A raced by Hamilton to victory in Turkey in 2010 sold for 4.8 million pounds in 2021 while a winning 2001 Ferrari raced by Michael Schumacher fetched $7.5 million in New York in 2017.

item.title: Flávio e Lula se enfrentam no primeiro debate; apoiadores ocupam as ruas
item.description: Brasileiros foram às ruas neste domingo em manifestações a favor e contra seus candidatos à Presidência, enquanto o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro se preparavam para seu primeiro debate televisionado, a uma semana do fim da campanha.
item.dc:creator: Brendan O'Boyle, Sebastian Recondio, Luis Nova
item.content:encoded: Brasileiros foram às ruas neste domingo em manifestações a favor e contra seus candidatos à Presidência, enquanto o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro se preparavam para seu primeiro debate televisionado, a uma semana do fim da campanha. Multidões pró-Bolsonaro, vestindo as cores nacionais do Brasil -- amarelo, verde e azul --, lotaram a Avenida Paulista, em São Paulo, onde o candidato discursou para os apoiadores. Apoiadores de Lula, vestidos de vermelho, cor simbólica do Partido dos Trabalhadores, lotaram a praça dos prédios do governo em Brasília, enquanto estudantes que apoiam o presidente protestaram contra Bolsonaro no Rio de Janeiro. As pesquisas mostram uma [USN:S0N45N09L TEXT:"disputa acirrada"] para o segundo turno de 25 de outubro, com Flávio, filho do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, mantendo uma ligeira vantagem após terminar quase 2 pontos percentuais à frente de Lula no [USN:L6N45N1A0 TEXT:"primeiro turno da eleição"], em 4 de outubro. Ambos os candidatos esperam conquistar os 33 milhões de eleitores que ficaram em casa no primeiro turno, o que equivale a cerca de um em cada cinco eleitores qualificados. O debate em São Paulo está marcado para começar às 20h e será transmitido pela emissora Band. O último debate do primeiro turno foi [USN:L1N45M12Z TEXT:"cancelado de última hora"], depois que Lula e Flávio desistiram de participar. Antes um marco da democracia brasileira após o fim da ditadura militar de 21 anos no país, em 1985, os debates presidenciais televisionados perderam relevância à medida que os principais candidatos passaram a optar cada vez mais por não participar. POLÍTICA ACIRRADA Espera-se que o debate entre Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula seja tenso e marcado por ataques pessoais. A polarização entre os apoiadores de Jair Bolsonaro e de Lula domina a política brasileira há quase uma década. Muitos bolsonaristas defendem que Lula deveria estar preso pelos escândalos de corrupção que envolveram o PT, enquanto muitos apoiadores de Lula argumentam que a condenação e a prisão do ex-presidente Bolsonaro por tentativa de golpe de Estado foram justificadas. "Eu não gosto de bandidos. Fora, Lula!", disse a manifestante Vera de Sousa, em São Paulo. No ato em São Paulo, participantes exibiam um grande boneco inflável de Lula vestido com roupa de presidiário. Já em Brasília, manifestantes entoavam gritos de "Bolsonaro na cadeia", enquanto uma imagem do ex-presidente o retratava com as mãos ensanguentadas. "Precisamos que o atual governo continue no poder. Se entrar outro governo, estamos, desculpe a expressão, ferrados", disse a apoiadora de Lula Sonia Maria, durante o ato em Brasília. Lula passou 580 dias preso entre 2018 e 2019 por uma condenação por corrupção que acabou sendo anulada devido a falhas nas investigações e nos procedimentos judiciais. Já o ex-presidente Bolsonaro foi condenado a 27 anos de prisão por conspirar para um golpe de Estado após perder a disputa pela reeleição para Lula em 2022. Ele cumpre a pena em prisão domiciliar por questões de saúde. O filho de Bolsonaro afirmou que o julgamento do pai foi uma "farsa" e prometeu buscar anistia para ele caso seja eleito presidente. "Faltam sete dias para livrarmos o Brasil do PT. E vocês verão Jair Messias Bolsonaro colocando a faixa de presidente no filho dele", disse Flávio à multidão em São Paulo. Em uma postagem na rede social X, Lula afirmou que quem votasse em seu oponente levaria, de "brinde", o pai e os irmãos dele. REVOLTA CONTRA META Uma polêmica sobre se as plataformas da Meta, que incluem o Facebook e o Instagram, trataram os dois candidatos de forma igualitária trouxe nova tensão aos últimos dias da campanha. A coalizão de Lula afirmou que sua conta no Instagram e suas publicações foram restringidas, e o jornal local Folha de S.Paulo divulgou mensagens internas de funcionários da Meta que admitiam [USN:S0N40000V TEXT:"essas restrições"] e afirmavam que a plataforma havia recomendado o perfil de Flávio e seu canal no WhatsApp aos usuários. A Meta afirmou ter enfrentado problemas técnicos globais, mas negou qualquer viés político. “Qualquer sugestão de que a Meta favoreça um lado é falsa”, disse a empresa. Organizações da sociedade civil planejavam realizar um protesto na segunda-feira em frente à sede da Meta em São Paulo contra a "interferência da empresa no processo eleitoral brasileiro", disseram os organizadores em comunicado. (Reportagem de Brendan O'Boyle e Luis Nova em Brasília, com reportagem adicional de Letícia Fucuchima e Sebastian Rocandio em São Paulo)

item.title: Milan police clash with protesters on second day of unrest
item.description: Milan police clashed on Sunday with protesters throwing stones and looting shops during demonstrations against poor services and the rising cost of living, a day after similar unrest in several Italian cities.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Milan police clashed on Sunday with protesters throwing stones and looting shops during demonstrations against poor services and the rising cost of living, a day after similar unrest in several Italian cities. Police in riot gear fired tear gas and used water cannons after several hundred hooded protesters broke shop windows and set bins on fire in the area near central Piazza Duomo, sources with knowledge of the investigation told Reuters. More than 60 protesters were taken to the police station for further checks, the sources added. A total of 28 protesters were arrested after similar clashes erupted on Saturday in northern cities including Milan, Bologna, Brescia, Bergamo and Turin, according to a police report on Sunday. The clashes had echoes of the [USN:L1N46401W TEXT:"violence in neighbouring France"], where hundreds of thousands of people angered by rising costs and declining public services took to the streets on Saturday in some of the country's most violent protests in years. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, facing an election next year, condemned the violence and announced a government meeting on Monday to discuss how to address the situation.

item.title: Barcelona Women suffer first defeat in 350 days
item.description: Barcelona's women suffered their first defeat in 350 days as Real Sociedad came from behind to claim a 2-1 Liga F victory at Zubieta on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Barcelona's women suffered their first defeat in 350 days as Real Sociedad came from behind to claim a 2-1 Liga F victory at Zubieta on Sunday. Patri Guijarro put Barcelona ahead inside the opening minute, but Cecilia Marcos equalised before Ainhoa Marin completed a memorable comeback for the Basque side. The defeat ended Barcelona's 45-game unbeaten run and was their first since a 1-0 loss to the same opponents last November. Barcelona lost only once last season as they swept the Champions League, Liga F, Copa de la Reina and Spanish Super Cup, while Sunday's setback was their first of the current campaign. They remain top of Liga F with 18 points, two ahead of second-placed Real Madrid, who beat Espanyol 3-1 on Saturday. Real Sociedad climbed to 11th on eight points after recording only their second victory of the season.

item.title: Papa Leão promete retorno gradual às funções no primeiro compromisso desde a cirurgia de câncer
item.description: O Papa Leão prometeu neste domingo retomar gradualmente suas atividades habituais como líder do 1,4 bilhão de católicos do mundo, ao saudar a multidão na Praça de São Pedro durante seu primeiro evento público desde que passou por uma cirurgia para tratar um câncer de pulmão, há cinco dias.
item.dc:creator: Joshua McElwee
item.content:encoded: O Papa Leão prometeu neste domingo retomar gradualmente suas atividades habituais como líder do 1,4 bilhão de católicos do mundo, ao saudar a multidão na Praça de São Pedro durante seu primeiro evento público desde que passou por uma cirurgia para tratar um câncer de pulmão, há cinco dias. O pontífice, de 71 anos, foi submetido a uma [USN:S8N42Y05U TEXT:"cirurgia"] na terça-feira para remover o lobo inferior do pulmão direito, [USN:L8N4600P9 TEXT:"o que alimentou especulações"] sobre como sua doença poderia alterar seus 17 meses de papado. Sorrindo de uma janela do Palácio Apostólico do Vaticano enquanto falava aos peregrinos abaixo com voz firme e clara neste domingo, o primeiro papa norte-americano agradeceu às pessoas de todo o mundo por suas orações e disse que agora começaria a retomar sua rotina normal. “Tendo superado essa fase delicada... agora retomarei gradualmente minhas atividades, sempre com a ajuda de Deus e de suas orações”, disse Leão. O papa, que recebeu alta do hospital Gemelli, em Roma, no sábado, chegou à janela do palácio sem ajuda e cumpriu seu compromisso semanal do meio-dia como de costume. Ele também exortou os peregrinos que aguardavam lá embaixo, sob um céu nublado, a deixarem de lado quaisquer ambições egoístas e a servirem a Deus “sem concessões”. FREIRA CHORA AO VER LEO APARECER Leão foi diagnosticado com [USN:L8N46006S TEXT:"adenocarcinoma de pulmão"], a forma mais comum de câncer de pulmão. O diagnóstico, para o papa mais jovem em décadas, eleito apenas em maio de 2025, causou comoção. Seus médicos deram alta a ele no sábado, depois que exames de sangue e imagens torácicas realizados naquele dia mostraram que ele estava bem o suficiente para voltar para casa. Os médicos afirmaram que ele era capaz de realizar atividades diárias normais de forma independente. A multidão na Praça de São Pedro, que somava cerca de 15 mil pessoas segundo o Vaticano, gritou e aplaudiu ruidosamente quando Leo apareceu pela primeira vez na janela no domingo. Uma freira católica se ajoelhou e chorou, cobrindo o rosto com as mãos. A poucos passos dali, um grupo de outras freiras erguia um cartaz com os dizeres: “Nossos melhores votos, Santo Padre. Nós o amamos e estamos rezando por você”. AGENDA DO PAPA EM MUDANÇA Leão costuma ter uma agenda lotada, mas o Vaticano cancelou seus outros eventos públicos até pelo menos quarta-feira, quando ele deve realizar uma audiência geral semanal na Praça de São Pedro. Não foi informado se ele realizará essa audiência. O papa também planeja visitar o Uruguai, a Argentina e o Peru de 6 a 17 de novembro, em uma das viagens mais intensas organizadas para um líder católico [USN:L8N45D0VL TEXT:"nas últimas décadas"]. O Dr. Stefano Margaritora, cirurgião-chefe do papa, disse no sábado que Leo poderia estar totalmente recuperado a tempo para essa viagem. O cardeal Pietro Parolin, secretário de Estado do Vaticano, expressou, no entanto, ceticismo. Ele disse a jornalistas na sexta-feira que o papa talvez precise ajustar o ritmo de sua agenda daqui para frente “de acordo com o estado de saúde”. (Reportagem de Joshua McElwee; Reportagem adicional de Matteo Minnella)

item.title: Ka'imi Fairbairn kicks Texans past Jaguars in London
item.description: CJ Stroud threw for 312 yards and three touchdowns to set the stage for Ka'imi Fairbairn's game-winning 49-yard field goal as time expired, helping the Houston Texans pull out a 34-31 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars Sunday in London.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: CJ Stroud threw for 312 yards and three touchdowns to set the stage for Ka'imi Fairbairn's game-winning 49-yard field goal as time expired, helping the Houston Texans pull out a 34-31 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars Sunday in London. Stroud completed 24 of 34 passes with one interception. Tight end Foster Moreau caught two passes, both touchdowns, while Jaylin Noel had a career-high 107 receiving yards and a touchdown for the Texans (2-4). Trevor Lawrence completed 24 of 41 passes for 306 yards, four touchdowns and one pick for the Jaguars (4-2), who had their three-game winning streak snapped. Bhayshul Tuten had 39 rushing yards and four catches for 48 yards and two TD catches. With Houston leading 31-28 late in the fourth quarter and driving toward a clinching score, Travis Hunter Jr. came away with an interception in the end zone. After he caught a touchdown pass on the prior possession, Hunter is the first NFL player since Brian Dawkins in 2002 with a TD catch and interception in the same game. That turnover set Cam Little up for a game-tying 60-yard field goal with 1:55 left. But Stroud found Woody Marks for a 19-yard gain to cross midfield, setting up Fairbairn's game-winner. Houston opened the scoring when Stroud connected with Moreau for a 6-yard score with 5:13 left in the first quarter. After a few squandered opportunities, the Jaguars leveled the score at 7-7 with 6:47 left in the first half on Lawrence's 27-yard connection with Tuten. The Texans responded with a 25-yard field goal from Fairbairn with 4:16 left in the first half, setting up a frantic finish to the first half. Lawrence found Tuten again, this time from 2 yards out, to give Jacksonville a 14-10 lead with 55 seconds left. However, a 50-yard pass from Stroud to Noel to begin the ensuing Houston drive set up a 1-yard TD catch by Moreau with eight seconds left to hand the Texans a 17-14 halftime edge. The back-and-forth blows continued in the second half, albeit with Houston keeping Jacksonville at arm's length. A 13-yard TD catch by Noel on the opening drive out of halftime gave the Texans a 24-14 lead. Lawrence found rookie tight end Nate Boerkircher for his first career TD to cut it to 24-21 with 2:34 left in the third. The Texans restored their two-score lead with Jawhar Jordan's 25-yard TD run. Jacksonville again responded with Lawrence finding Hunter for a 7-yard score to cut it to 31-28. --Field Level Media

item.title: Big 12 admits clock error in Notre Dame's loss to BYU
item.description: The Big 12 acknowledged that one second should have been placed back on the clock after what turned out to be the final play of the Notre Dame-BYU game on Saturday in Provo, Utah.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Big 12 acknowledged that one second should have been placed back on the clock after what turned out to be the final play of the Notre Dame-BYU game on Saturday in Provo, Utah. With four seconds remaining on the clock, Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr tossed an incomplete pass to Jaden Greathouse in the right corner of the end zone. Replays showed the ball hit the ground with one second remaining, but the clock still ran out in No. 8 BYU's 28-24 victory over No. 2 Notre Dame. "Following the Big 12's review of the final play of Saturday's Notre Dame-BYU game, it was determined that time remained on the clock when the ball hit the ground," the Big 12's statement read, "and the play was incorrectly cleared by the replay officiating crew. "The Conference will conduct a complete review of its end-of-game officiating process in advance of next week's games." As an FBS independent, Notre Dame has its games officiated by the conference of its opponent. --Field Level Media

WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Sunday (Oct 18) endorsed his ally Benjamin Netanyahu as the longtime Israeli prime minister struggles for an edge in next week's parliamentary election. Trump praised Netanyahu as a "great warrior prime minster" and peace partner, crediting him with joining the United States in launching strikes on Iran in February. The conflict, in its seventh month, has disrupted energy markets globally and wreaked havoc across the Middle East, damaging critical infrastructure and destabilising regional economies. "Bibi Netanyahu has been Strong, Brave, and Brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself," Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social. "Despite all of that, he has endured and, in fact, he has thrived! I have watched Bibi under the most trying of times. Normal men or women in such situations would have wilted under the pressure - But Bibi did not wilt, he actually got stronger, and maintains that same Strength today."

Show Less

In his message, addressed to "the Great People of Israel," Trump added, "Please let this Letter serve to represent my Complete and Total Endorsement of Bibi Netanyahu in his upcoming Race for Re-Election as Prime Minister of Israel." The Trump endorsement is not certain to give Netanyahu and his right-wing Likud party a boost in the Oct 27 national election, as Israeli public support for Trump has diminished amid Israeli-US disagreements over Iran.

Related:

Trump rules out new Iran attack before US midterm elections

Israel top court puts Arab parties back on ballot

Polls have suggested no candidate has a clear path to power. Israel's prime minister is chosen through coalition-building in parliament rather than by direct popular vote. It will be Israel's first vote since the Hamas attack on Oct 7, 2023, that shook the country and plunged the Middle East into turmoil, as Israel went to war in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. The election could determine whether Netanyahu remains in power after one of the most consequential periods in Israel’s history, or is defeated by centrist rivals promising to usher in a new era. Netanyahu promptly expressed his thanks to Trump on X, saying, "Together we will complete the mission!" Trump has broken with longtime US tradition by endorsing candidates in elections in foreign countries, including Hungary, Colombia, Argentina, Japan and Honduras.

Source: Reuters/fs

item.title: Brazil's Bolsonaro, Lula face off in first debate as supporters fill streets
item.description: Brazilians demonstrated for and against their presidential candidates on Sunday as President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro prepared to meet in their first televised debate with just one week left in the campaign.
item.dc:creator: Brendan O'Boyle, Sebastian Recondio, Luis Nova
item.content:encoded: Brazilians demonstrated for and against their presidential candidates on Sunday as President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro prepared to meet in their first televised debate with just one week left in the campaign. Pro-Bolsonaro crowds wearing Brazil's national colors of yellow, green and blue packed Paulista Avenue in Sao Paulo's financial center, where the candidate addressed the crowd. Lula supporters wearing red, symbolic of his Workers' Party, filled Brasilia's plaza of government buildings, and students backing the president protested against Bolsonaro in Rio de Janeiro. Polls show a [USN:S0N45N09L TEXT:"close race"] for the October 25 runoff, with Bolsonaro, son of former far-right President Jair Bolsonaro, holding a slight advantage after finishing nearly 2 percentage points ahead of leftist Lula in the [USN:L6N45N1A0 TEXT:"election's first round"] on October 4. Both candidates hope to engage the 33 million voters who stayed home in the election's first round, equal to about one in five eligible voters. The debate in Sao Paulo is scheduled to begin at 8 p.m. (2300 GMT) and air on broadcaster Band. The last debate in the election's first round was [USN:L1N45M12Z TEXT:"canceled at the last minute"] when Lula and Bolsonaro pulled out. Once a hallmark of Brazilian democracy following the end of the country's 21-year military dictatorship in 1985, televised presidential debates have lost relevance as leading candidates have increasingly chosen to stay away. BITTER POLITICS The debate between Senator Bolsonaro and President Lula is expected to be tense and personal. Bitter polarization between supporters of the elder Bolsonaro and Lula has dominated Brazilian politics for nearly a decade. Many Bolsonaro supporters believe Lula should be jailed over corruption scandals that ensnared his Workers' Party, while many Lula backers argue former President Bolsonaro's conviction and imprisonment for a coup attempt were warranted. "I don't like bandits. Out with Lula!" said demonstrator Vera de Sousa in Sao Paulo. At the Sao Paulo rally, crowd members held aloft a large inflatable of Lula in a prisoner's uniform, while rallygoers in Brasilia chanted "Bolsonaro in jail" and an effigy of Bolsonaro showed the former president with bloody hands. "We need the current government to remain in power. If another government comes in, we're, excuse my language, screwed," said Lula supporter Sonia Maria at the Brasilia rally. Lula spent 580 days in prison in 2018-2019 for a corruption conviction that was later overturned because of flaws in the investigations and legal proceedings. Former President Bolsonaro, meanwhile, received a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup after losing his reelection bid to Lula in 2022. He is serving that underhouse arrest due to health issues. The younger Bolsonaro has said his father's trial was a "farce" and has promised to seek amnesty for him if elected president. "There are seven days left until we free Brazil from (Lula's) Workers’ Party. And you will see Jair Messias Bolsonaro placing the presidential sash on his son," Bolsonaro told the crowd in Sao Paulo. In a post on X, Lula said that anyone who voted for his opponent would get his father and brothers as a "bonus gift." ANGER OVER META A dispute over whether Meta’s platforms, which include Facebook and Instagram, treated the two candidates equally has injected new tension into the campaign's final days. Lula’s coalition said his Instagram account and posts were restricted, and local newspaper Folha de S.Paulo reported internal Meta messages that acknowledged [USN:S0N40000V TEXT:"those restrictions"] and said the platform had recommended Bolsonaro’s profile and WhatsApp channel to users. Meta said it had experienced global technical glitches but denied any political bias. “Any suggestion that Meta favors one side is false,” the company said. Civil society groups were planning a protest for Monday at Meta's main office in Sao Paulo, against "the company’s interference in the Brazilian electoral process," its organizers said in a press release.

item.title: Trump respalda a Netanyahu en las elecciones de Israel
item.description: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, respaldó este domingo a su aliado Benjamin Netanyahu, mientras el veterano primer ministro israelí lucha por hacerse con ventaja de cara a las elecciones parlamentarias de la próxima semana.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, respaldó este domingo a su aliado Benjamin Netanyahu, mientras el veterano primer ministro israelí lucha por hacerse con ventaja de cara a las elecciones parlamentarias de la próxima semana. Trump elogió a Netanyahu como un "gran primer ministro guerrero" y socio por la paz, y le reconoció el mérito de haberse unido a EEUU en los ataques contra Irán llevados a cabo en febrero. El conflicto, que ya cumple siete meses, ha trastornado los mercados energéticos a nivel mundial y ha causado estragos en todo Oriente Medio, dañando infraestructuras críticas y desestabilizando las economías regionales. "Bibi Netanyahu se ha mostrado fuerte, valiente y brillante frente a una tremenda oposición, incluida la procedente incluso del propio Israel", escribió Trump en una publicación en Truth Social. "A pesar de todo ello, ha resistido y, de hecho, ¡ha salido airoso! He observado a Bibi en los momentos más difíciles. Cualquier hombre o mujer normal en tales situaciones se habría derrumbado bajo la presión, pero Bibi no se derrumbó; de hecho, se hizo más fuerte y mantiene esa misma fortaleza hoy en día". En su mensaje, dirigido al "gran pueblo de Israel", Trump añadió: "Que esta carta sirva para expresar mi apoyo total y absoluto a Bibi Netanyahu en su próxima campaña para la reelección como primer ministro de Israel". No es seguro que el respaldo de Trump suponga un impulso para Netanyahu y su partido de derecha, el Likud, en las elecciones nacionales del 27 de octubre, ya que el apoyo público israelí a Trump ha disminuido en medio de los desacuerdos entre Israel y EEUU sobre Irán. Las encuestas sugieren que ningún candidato tiene un camino claro hacia el poder. El primer ministro de Israel se elige mediante la formación de una coalición en el Parlamento, y no por voto popular directo. Serán las primeras elecciones en Israel desde el ataque de Hamás del 7 de octubre de 2023, que sacudió al país y sumió a Oriente Medio en el caos, al entrar Israel en guerra en Gaza, el Líbano e Irán. Las elecciones podrían determinar si Netanyahu permanece en el poder tras uno de los períodos más trascendentales de la historia de Israel, o si es derrotado por rivales centristas que prometen marcar el comienzo de una nueva era. Netanyahu no tardó en expresar su agradecimiento a Trump en X, afirmando: "¡Juntos completaremos la misión!". Trump ha roto con una larga tradición estadounidense al respaldar a candidatos en elecciones de países extranjeros, entre ellos Hungría, Colombia, Argentina, Japón y Honduras. El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, expresó el domingo su apoyo a su aliado Benjamin Netanyahu de cara a las próximas elecciones parlamentarias israelíes.

item.title: Captain of flydubai plane describes blocking axe blows as co-pilot attacked
item.description: The captain of a flydubai flight who was attacked by a co-pilot who intended to crash the plane has described blocking axe blows to the head and screaming for help as he reached for a knob to open the cockpit door.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The captain of a flydubai flight who was attacked by a co-pilot who intended to crash the plane has described blocking axe blows to the head and screaming for help as he reached for a knob to open the cockpit door. Captain Smit Machchhar has been hailed as a hero for his role in averting disaster on the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv last month, helping to thwart what the UAE attorney general has said was an [USN:L6N45V0UP TEXT:"attempted suicide attack"] by the co-pilot who intended to crash the plane into Ben Gurion Airport. Speaking in an interview with The National newspaper from a hospital bed in Abu Dhabi, his head and left arm bandaged, Machchhar said that when the first blow landed, he thought something had gone "horribly wrong the aircraft structure", before quickly realising he was being attacked and things had "taken a drastic turn". "The next thought was I need to get help in here," he said in the interview published on Saturday. "My immediate action was to free myself from the seat belts and I tried to just block the blows as much as I could," he said, pointing to his arm that was wounded as he defended himself. "The blows were coming on the head." "Immediately my hand went to the knob which opens the door and screaming for my colleagues, screaming his name." "I believe that was the first time when I lost my consciousness." The aircraft, flight FZ1073, was in Saudi airspace when the co-pilot attacked Machchhar with a crash axe, typically kept in the cockpit for emergency use. The incident caused the airliner to plunge 16,000 feet (4,900 meters) in 30 seconds before the attacker was overwhelmed and two other pilots who were on board landed the aircraft safely in Saudi Arabia. The suspect, an Omani national, was transferred to the UAE, flydubai's home country. The plan was inspired by the September 11, 2001, attacks on the US, UAE public prosecutors say, as a result of their criminal investigation launched on October 1. Machchhar said he heard the cockpit door opening and screaming "between my colleague and the guy". He said the scariest thing he felt was the aircraft nose "steeply going down." "I was not very sure that I'll make it out alive from this. Did I give up? No."

item.title: Tensões voltam a crescer em Paris enquanto França contabiliza os custos da pior onda de distúrbios em anos
item.description: Novos confrontos eclodiram em Paris neste domingo, um dia depois de a França ter vivido um dos piores dias de agitação dos últimos anos, com protestos contra os preços altos que deixaram um manifestante morto, milhares de pessoas presas e lojas saqueadas ou danificadas em todo o país.
item.dc:creator: Sybille de La Hamaide
item.content:encoded: Novos confrontos eclodiram em Paris neste domingo, um dia depois de a França ter vivido um dos piores dias de agitação dos últimos anos, com protestos contra os preços altos que deixaram um manifestante morto, milhares de pessoas presas e lojas saqueadas ou danificadas em todo o país. Manifestações em todo o país se transformaram em tumultos no sábado, com uma prefeitura incendiada, lojas saqueadas e prédios cobertos de pichações, enquanto grupos violentos entraram em confronto com a polícia em cidades por todo o país. Um manifestante morreu após sofrer uma parada cardíaca durante [USN:L1N46302B TEXT:"os protestos"] em Paris. A polícia realizou mais de 2.000 prisões em toda a França, enquanto mais de 600 policiais ficaram feridos, informou o ministro do Interior. “Aqui parece uma zona de guerra”, disse o empresário holandês Tije De Boer, que havia vindo a Paris com seus filhos para visitar um amigo e afirmou que os protestos o forçaram a evacuar seu hotel na Place de la République, um dos pontos mais conturbados no sábado. A polícia voltou a lançar gás lacrimogêneo contra os manifestantes na Place de la République e bicicletas foram incendiadas na tarde de domingo, um sinal de que as tensões ainda não haviam se acalmado totalmente na capital. Mais de meio milhão de pessoas participaram de marchas em dezenas de cidades no sábado, marcando a convergência de um [USN:L6N45M1EJ TEXT:"movimento estudantil"] que já dura um mês com um descontentamento social mais amplo contra o aumento do custo de vida e o declínio dos serviços públicos. O presidente Emmanuel Macron fará um pronunciamento à nação às 20h, horário local, no domingo, informou seu gabinete. Os distúrbios de sábado revelaram a profunda raiva contra Macron, que deixará o cargo em 2027 após uma década no poder cada vez mais marcada pelo descontentamento social, uma economia fraca e uma dívida galopante. O governo atribuiu a violência a grupos de extrema esquerda e ultra-esquerda, bem como a criminosos que, segundo o governo, instigaram os saques. O líder da extrema direita francesa, Jordan Bardella, afirmou que a França havia sido “humilhada” e pediu que Macron renunciasse. “Estamos pagando por décadas de negligência, perda de autoridade e pelo desarmamento moral, psicológico e material de nossas forças de segurança interna”, disse ele durante visita a uma delegacia de polícia em Paris. VÁRIAS CENTENAS DE LOJAS DANIFICADAS Enquanto centenas de milhares protestavam pacificamente, grupos marginais violentos atacaram prédios públicos, saquearam butiques de luxo e supermercados e atacaram veículos e policiais. Uma operação maciça de limpeza teve início em cidades que vão de Lille, no norte, a Marselha, no sul, e de Estrasburgo, no leste, a Bordeaux, no sudoeste, onde uma multidão mascarada invadiu a residência do prefeito local. O ministro do Interior, Laurent Nunez, afirmou que várias centenas de lojas foram danificadas no sábado. Em [USN:L1N46402C TEXT:"Limoges"], no sudoeste da França, o prefeito Guillaume Guerin denunciou o caos após a prefeitura da cidade, de 143 anos, ter sido incendiada e amplamente destruída em um ataque criminoso no sábado, o que gerou comparações com o incêndio de 2019 que devastou a Catedral de Notre-Dame, em Paris. “Houve uma intenção clara e premeditada de incendiar a prefeitura, e as pessoas que estavam lá dentro temeram por suas vidas”, disse Guerin à Reuters. Ele ameaçou renunciar caso a cidade não recebesse os recursos necessários para reparar a prefeitura. ELEIÇÃO PRESIDENCIAL ACONTECERÁ NO PRÓXIMO ANO Os distúrbios aumentaram a pressão sobre o presidente Macron e seu governo antes da eleição presidencial prevista para o próximo ano. O primeiro-ministro Sébastien Lecornu atribuiu os distúrbios à “extrema esquerda” e aos criminosos. O ministro da Economia, Roland Lescure, prometeu apoio no domingo aos empresários que sofreram prejuízos. “Quem destruir coisas vai pagar, reparar os danos e ser responsabilizado por sua intenção de semear o caos”, disse Lescure em comunicado. O prefeito de Bordeaux, Thomas Cazenave, disse que até 100 lojas foram saqueadas em sua cidade, enquanto o prefeito de Marselha, Benoit Payan, anunciou ajuda financeira de emergência para apoiar as empresas afetadas pela violência. O presidente-executivo da rede francesa de varejo Carrefour (CARR.PA) , Alexandre Bompard, disse à emissora francesa BFMTV que 50 lojas da empresa foram danificadas, incluindo 20 que foram saqueadas, com prejuízos decorrentes dos danos chegando a dezenas de milhões de euros. Os protestos começaram no mês passado devido às condições das escolas e à escassez de professores nos subúrbios da classe trabalhadora, antes de se transformarem em um movimento contra a desigualdade, os cortes nos gastos públicos e o aumento do custo de vida. (Reportagem de Sybille de La Hamaide; Reportagem adicional de Natasa Bansagi, Janis Laizans, Abdul Saboor e Clotaire Achi)

item.title: Trump apporte son soutien à Netanyahu pour les élections en Israël
item.description: Le président américain Donald Trump a apporté dimanche son soutien à Benjamin Netanyahu en vue des prochaines élections législatives israéliennes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le président américain Donald Trump a apporté dimanche son soutien à Benjamin Netanyahu en vue des prochaines élections législatives israéliennes. "Bibi Netanyahu s’est montré fort, courageux et brillant face à une opposition farouche, y compris celle venant d’Israël même", a écrit Donald Trump dans un message publié sur son réseau Truth Social. "C’est le genre de partenaire que les États-Unis d’Amérique attendent d’Israël, un pays pour lequel ils ont tant fait. Que cette lettre témoigne de mon soutien total et inconditionnel à Bibi Netanyahu dans sa prochaine campagne pour sa réélection au poste de Premier ministre d’Israël." Les élections législatives se dérouleront le 27 octobre. Il s'agira du premier scrutin depuis les attaques du Hamas le 7 octobre 2023 et la coalition au pouvoir apparaît en difficulté dans les sondages d'intention de vote.
