item.title: Egypt says ready to back Saudi Arabia in war against Iran-allied Houthis
item.description: Regional military power Egypt is ready to provide Saudi Arabia with the support it needs to defend its security and stability, the presidency said on Sunday, potentially raising the stakes in the Middle East war as Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis intensify their attacks on the kingdom.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Regional military power Egypt is ready to provide Saudi Arabia with the support it needs to defend its security and stability, the presidency said on Sunday, potentially raising the stakes in the Middle East war as Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis intensify their attacks on the kingdom. Egyptian President [USN:L8N46306J TEXT:"Abdel Fattah al-Sisi"] requested an urgent parliament session to authorise the military, one of the Arab world's largest, to help defend its Gulf Arab ally if the kingdom requested its support. A parliamentary vote had been expected on Sunday, but discussions were due to continue on Monday, two lawmakers and local media reports said. Fighting between the Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's internationally recognised government and the Houthis, who control the capital Sanaa and much of the north, has escalated in recent weeks, becoming another front in the US-Israeli war on Iran . Any Egyptian military backing for Saudi Arabia could mark a major escalation in the wider Iran war, which has threatened global energy supplies and sent oil prices soaring since the US and Israel attacked the Islamic Republic in late February. Hours after an announcement on further discussions by the parliament, Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said in a post on X that he discussed regional developments and the importance of de-escalation during a phone call with his Saudi counterpart, Prince Faisal bin Farhan. HOUTHIS RAMP UP ATTACKS ON SAUDI ARABIA The Houthis have in recent days attacked [USN:S8N44Y00K TEXT:"Riyadh's international airport"] and the state oil company [USN:S8N44D022 TEXT:"Saudi Aramco"], amid renewed fighting with Saudi-backed forces. The Houthi advances threaten the strategic Bab el-Mandeb oil shipping route, following the collapse of a truce. "Egypt will provide Saudi Arabia with all necessary and possible forms of support to defend its security and stability, protect its resources, territorial integrity and Islamic holy sites," the Egyptian presidency said in a statement. The statement followed a meeting of Egypt's National Defence Council chaired by Sisi and attended by the parliamentary speaker, the prime minister and the army chief. Sisi said in a [USN:L8N46306J TEXT:"speech"] on Saturday that Egypt would act in accordance with guidance from Saudi King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, who visited Sisi on September 15, after fighting in Yemen reignited. If Egypt weighs in, it could face attacks by the Houthis, ragtag mountain fighters who have emerged as a deadly force of tens of thousands and whose missiles and drones threaten the region. Arab countries, especially Gulf states hosting US bases, have faced [USN:L6N4610JI TEXT:"repeated attacks by Iran"] and its allies, including the Houthis and pro-Iranian militias in Iraq, during the conflict. Egypt's Mediterranean port of Damietta came under a drone attack [USN:L1N43W0P5 TEXT:"in July"] with no group claiming responsibility. Egypt has not blamed any party for the attack but said it was taking necessary measures to protect the country's national security. Egypt and Saudi Arabia are close strategic and economic partners. Saudi Arabia and other oil-rich Gulf states including the United Arab Emirates provided Egypt with billions of dollars in aid, central-bank deposits and investments after the military ouster of Islamist President Mohamed Morsi in 2013. Sisi became president a year later. Egypt had previously joined the Saudi-led coalition that intervened in Yemen in 2015 to support the government against the Houthis, but played a limited combat role in the civil war. Riyadh has turned to regional allies and Pakistan after it [USN:P8N3ZN0LL TEXT:"sought"] US President Donald Trump's help to fight the Houthis. Trump did not agree to US strikes, sources told Reuters last month. Washington instead offered targeting assistance and intelligence-sharing. Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman visited Abu Dhabi on Sunday and met with UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, with talks focusing on regional security, according to the Emirati state news agency. The talks followed a visit to Riyadh last month by UAE Vice President Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the first trip by a senior UAE official to the kingdom since a deep rift emerged between the two Gulf powers last year.

item.title: Roy Cooper's North Carolina playbook is working. Can other Democrats copy it?
item.description: North Carolina hasn’t elected a Democrat to the Senate in nearly 20 years, but former Governor Roy Cooper, who hasn't lost an election in four decades, has built a double-digit lead over Republican Michael Whatley.
item.dc:creator: Yasmeen Abutaleb
item.content:encoded: North Carolina hasn’t elected a Democrat to the US Senate in nearly 20 years, but former Governor Roy Cooper has built a double-digit lead over Republican Michael Whatley by relentlessly focusing on affordability and a blunt promise to “make stuff cost less.” At campaign stops, Cooper, 69, points to his six-year fight to expand Medicaid through a Republican-controlled legislature as evidence he can work across party lines, while attacking Trump-backed healthcare cuts that he says are hitting North Carolinians hard. “People should not have to make a choice between going to a doctor and putting food on the table,” Cooper said at a September 26 rally in Raleigh, North Carolina. “This 'Big Beautiful Bill' that gave tax cuts to billionaires has now driven healthcare premiums up more than double for people.” The White House says the bill cuts taxes, protects Medicaid for eligible Americans and curbs fraud and abuse. Cooper's message appears to be working: His lead stood at 14 points in an October SurveyUSA poll. The top super PAC for Senate Republicans has paused TV advertising in North Carolina less than three weeks before the election and begun shifting campaign dollars to defend seats in states that include Iowa and Kansas. President Donald Trump will rally in the state on Tuesday for Whatley, a former Republican National Committee chair who has never held elected office. The question for Democrats is whether Cooper's playbook can help them win Republican and independent voters elsewhere, or whether his success is unique to a popular former governor who has never lost an election in four decades of public service. While some Democrats in heavily Democratic states have embraced Medicare for All, which would provide government-run health insurance for all Americans, Cooper has focused on expanding existing coverage and lowering costs. He points to his fight to expand Medicaid, the government health insurance program for low-income Americans, and campaigns on prescription drug and insurance costs. 'OUR STAR ATHLETE AND NO ONE'S PAYING ANY ATTENTION' “It’s like he’s our star athlete and no one’s paying any attention,” said Neera Tanden, president of the Center for American Progress, a Democratic-aligned think tank, and former White House adviser to President Joe Biden. “The strength of Roy Cooper’s campaign is that he’s able to attract Democrats and independents, but also even some Republicans because he’s focused on cost, but he also has a record.” Paul Shumaker, a longtime Republican strategist in North Carolina, attributes Cooper’s success to the fact he was already well-known and that Whatley failed to distinguish himself from Trump. “Roy Cooper came to the US Senate race with a known brand that has been trusted by a majority of North Carolina voters election after election,” Shumaker said. “Republicans are suffering from a lack of trust on the economy right now and Whatley has failed to reestablish that trust.” Cooper declined an interview request for this story. The Whatley campaign did not respond to a request for comment, but on Sunday he predicted victory during an interview with Fox News. Trump's upcoming visit to North Carolina and an expected rally with Vice President JD Vance will energize Republican voters, Whatley told Fox News' "Sunday Briefing." "Our election is going to come down to turnout and we're in a state that President Trump won three straight times," Whatley said. WINNING OVER INDEPENDENTS North Carolina’s electorate is unusually independent: 40% of registered voters are unaffiliated with either party, compared with 30% each for Republicans and Democrats. Republicans, however, have dominated the state legislature for more than a decade and redrawn districts to strengthen their grip. Like other Republican candidates, Whatley must contend with Trump’s record-low approval rating, which now hovers at 32%, according to an October [USN:L6N45R10Y TEXT:"Reuters/Ipsos poll"]. That poll also showed registered voters preferring Democrats over Republicans nationally by 44% to 37%. Among independents, Democrats led 37% to 21%, with 28% of independent voters still undecided. Republicans hold a 53-47 majority in the US Senate, where Democrats must net four seats in the November 3 midterm elections to control the chamber — an already difficult task that makes Cooper's North Carolina race especially important. Cooper's signature bipartisan achievement did not come easily. It took him six years to persuade the Republican-controlled state legislature to pass an expansion of Medicaid under Obamacare in 2023, extending health insurance to more than 700,000 state residents, according to state health department data. After passage, he called it “an unnecessarily long and agonizing journey.” Whit Ayres, a Republican pollster, said several moderate Democratic governors in the South could replicate Cooper’s success, including Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear. “The Roy Coopers of the world are not unique,” Ayres said. “The Republicans nominated someone who’s never been elected to any public office at any level anywhere running against a reasonably moderate, popular governor.” RUNNING AGAINST HEALTHCARE CUTS Many of the state’s Medicaid gains are likely to be undone by Trump’s “One Big Beautiful Bill,” a sweeping tax and budget bill the Republican-led Congress passed last year that cuts about $1 trillion from Medicaid, the largest cut in the program’s history, according to the nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office. Cooper has used Trump’s signature domestic legislative achievement to paint the president and Republicans as depriving North Carolinians of healthcare in order to give billionaires more tax cuts. He has also focused on congressional Republicans’ decision to curtail COVID-era Obamacare subsidies last year, causing healthcare premiums on the individual health insurance marketplace to spike and more than 200,000 state residents to drop their coverage, according to health policy research firm KFF. “Roy Cooper has always polled over Republicans,” said Anderson Clayton, chair of the North Carolina Democratic Party. “This will be the average election for Roy Cooper.”

item.description: Microsoft reportedly ended its agreement for Nscale's Loughton data centre amid power delays, while the cloud provider said its other contracts with Microsoft were unaffected ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / Microsoft exits Nscale data centre deal in UK amid power delays: Report

Microsoft exits Nscale data centre deal in UK amid power delays: Report Microsoft reportedly ended its agreement for Nscale's Loughton data centre amid power delays, while the cloud provider said its other contracts with Microsoft were unaffected

Nscale provides infrastructure, including compute, power and data centres, as well as software for training and running AI models | Image: Bloomberg

Reuters 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 18 2026 | 10:32 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Microsoft has pulled out of a data centre deal with British cloud provider Nscale, Britain's Telegraph newspaper reported on Sunday.   The US tech giant, one of Nscale's two largest customers, recently terminated its agreement for the data centre in Loughton, Essex, according to the report.   The newspaper did not specify why Microsoft withdrew from the project. Microsoft declined a Reuters request for comment.   The Telegraph report said Nscale had faced repeated delays with the project. National power grid officials, it reported, had told Nscale they did not expect a power supply for the data centre until the 2030s.   "Our relationship with Microsoft remains strong and long-term, and this unfortunate London-wide grid issue has no impact on our other contracts," an Nscale spokesperson told Reuters.

Also Read

AdaniConneX's Vizag data centres to use air cooling, limit freshwater use

InvoiceCloud strengthens global innovation hub in India with ₹350 cr

As campus placements near, old IITs see rising demand for AI talent

"We remain committed to both the Loughton project and the UK, and we are exploring alternative power sources for the site, in addition to other expansion sites in the UK." Nscale filed for an initial public offering in the US last month, with Microsoft and Anthropic expected to be its major customers, according to its prospectus.   Nscale provides infrastructure, including compute, power and data centres, as well as software for training and running AI models.   The Nvidia-backed AI group, which competes against CoreWeave, Nebius, Crusoe and Lambda, has grown rapidly since its launch, scaling from $100 million to more than $103 billion in total contracted value in just two and a half years.

item.title: Macron urges calm as France counts cost of worst unrest in years
item.description: The French president appealed for calm a day after France suffered one of its worst days of unrest in years, with thousands arrested and shops looted or damaged after protests over high prices and declining public services.
item.dc:creator: Sybille de La Hamaide, Clotaire Achi, Abdul Saboor
item.content:encoded: President Emmanuel Macron appealed for calm on Sunday, a day after France suffered one of its worst days of unrest in years, with thousands arrested and shops looted or damaged after protests over high prices and declining public services. Fresh clashes broke out in Paris and Marseille, where riot police intervened to prevent attempts to ransack businesses. Nationwide demonstrations had erupted into riots on Saturday, with a town hall torched, shops pillaged and buildings covered in graffiti as violent groups clashed with police in cities across the country. "Looking at these images, we have all asked ourselves: What was going through their minds? How can French people do this to France?" Macron said in a televised address to the nation. "Nothing justifies it, nothing explains it, nothing excuses it. Tonight, we all feel anger and shame." Saturday's unrest laid bare the deep anger at Macron, who leaves office in 2027 after a decade in power that has increasingly become defined by social discontent, a weak economy and ballooning debt. Macron said those protesting peacefully had legitimate grievances and their actions should not be confused with those seeking to wreak havoc. He stopped short of declaring a state of emergency, as demanded by some right-wing politicians, but said the government would act to allow prefects to ban protests if necessary to protect public buildings and local businesses. PARIS PROTESTS 'LIKE A WAR ZONE' The government has blamed the violence on what it said were ultra-left groups, as well as criminals it said had instigated the looting. One protester died on Saturday after suffering a cardiac arrest during [USN:L1N46302B TEXT:"demonstrations"] in Paris. Police made 2,400 arrests across France, while nearly 1,000 officers were injured, French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said. Police again clashed with protesters and fired tear gas at Place de la Republique on Sunday afternoon, and protesters had set fire to piles of bicycles. A Reuters witness said there appeared to be several hundred protesters in the area. A massive clean-up operation took place in cities from Lille in the north to Marseille in the south and from Strasbourg in the east to Bordeaux in the southwest, where a masked mob invaded the residence of the local prefect. "It's like a war zone here!" exclaimed Dutch entrepreneur Tije De Boer, who was visiting Paris with his children and said the unrest forced him to evacuate his hotel at Place de la Republique. More than half a million people joined marches in scores of cities on Saturday, marking the convergence of a month-long [USN:L6N45M1EJ TEXT:"student movement"] with broader social discontent against rising living costs and declining public services. SEVERAL HUNDRED SHOPS DAMAGED While hundreds of thousands protested peacefully across France on Saturday, violent fringe groups targeted public buildings, looted luxury boutiques and supermarkets, and attacked police vehicles and officers. Far-right National Rally leader Marine Le Pen, frontrunner going into next year's presidential campaign, also called for calm, saying France must not become accustomed to images of the country being battered, abused and ransacked. "Violence is not an opinion. Destruction is not a form of expression. And chaos cannot serve as a project for France," she said in a video address. Hard-left France Unbowed presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon said Macron needed to answer the demands of protesting high-school students. In [USN:L1N46402C TEXT:"Limoges"], famed for its porcelain, the collapse of the town hall's clock tower in a fiery blaze revived memories of the 2019 fire that devastated Paris' Notre Dame cathedral. Mayor Guillaume Guerin said not enough officers from the national police had been deployed to his city. "There was a clear, premeditated intention to burn down the town hall, and the people inside feared for their lives," Guerin told Reuters on Sunday. He threatened to resign if the city did not receive the funds needed to repair the town hall. Economy Minister Roland Lescure pledged support on Sunday for business owners who suffered losses. "Those who break things will pay, repair the damage and be held accountable for their intention to sow chaos," Lescure said in a statement. French retailer Carrefour's (CARR.PA) CEO Alexandre Bompard told French broadcaster BFMTV that 50 of the company's shops had been damaged, including 20 that were looted, with losses from the damage running into the tens of millions of euros.

item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / France reels after riots leave one dead, over 2,000 arrested nationwide

France reels after riots leave one dead, over 2,000 arrested nationwide Riots over high prices and declining public services damaged hundreds of shops and injured more than 600 police officers, as Macron prepared to address the nation on Sunday

Fire in Limoges city hall amid protests, in Limoges, France, October 17, 2026, in this screengrab from a video obtained from social media. Lucas Destrem/via Reuters

Reuters Paris 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 18 2026 | 9:29 PM IST

Listen to This Article

France reeled on Sunday from one of its most violent days of unrest in years after protests over high prices and public services left one demonstrator dead, thousands arrested and hundreds of police injured.   Nationwide demonstrations erupted into riots on Saturday, with a town hall torched, shops ransacked and buildings covered in graffiti as violent groups clashed with police in cities across the country.   One protester died after suffering a cardiac arrest during demonstrations in Paris. Police made more than 2,000 arrests across France, while more than 600 officers were injured, the interior minister said.   "It's like a war zone here," said Dutch entrepreneur Tije De Boer, who had come to Paris with his children to visit a friend and said the protests forced him to evacuate his hotel at Place de la Republique, a trouble hotspot on Saturday.

More than half a million people joined marches in scores of cities, marking the convergence of a month-long student movement with broader social discontent over rising living costs and declining public services. Also Read

Mass demonstrations in France spiral into worst violence in decades

Cyberattack targets French supermarket fridges, sparks fires, spoils food

France confers highest civilian honour on Bharti Enterprises' Sunil Mittal

Why are thousands of French students protesting across the country?

France plans trials of AI-powered 'wingmen' for Rafale jets by 2028

President Emmanuel Macron will address the nation at 8 pm local time (1800 GMT) on Sunday, his office said.   Saturday's unrest laid bare the deep anger at Macron, who leaves office in 2027 after a decade in power that has increasingly become defined by social discontent, a weak economy and ballooning debt.   The government has blamed the violence on hard-left and ultra-left groups, as well as criminals who it said instigated the looting.

Several hundred shops damaged   While hundreds of thousands protested peacefully, violent fringe groups targeted public buildings, looted luxury boutiques and supermarkets, and attacked police vehicles and officers.   A massive clean-up operation began in cities from Lille in the north to Marseille in the south and Strasbourg in the east to Bordeaux in the south-west, where a masked mob invaded the residence of the local prefect.   Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said several hundred shops had been damaged on Saturday.   In Paris, smashed shop windows, burnt-out bicycles and spray-painted slogans bore witness to a day that began largely with peaceful demonstrations but descended into violence.   In Limoges, south-western France, Mayor Guillaume Guerin denounced the chaos after the city's 143-year-old town hall was set ablaze and largely destroyed in an arson attack on Saturday, drawing comparisons to the 2019 fire that devastated Paris's Notre-Dame Cathedral.

"There was a clear, premeditated intention to burn down the town hall, and the people inside feared for their lives," Guerin told Reuters. He threatened to resign if the city did not receive the funds needed to repair the town hall.   Presidential election to take place next year   The unrest has increased pressure on President Macron and his government ahead of a presidential election due next year.   Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu blamed the unrest on the "ultra-left" and criminals.   Economy Minister Roland Lescure pledged support on Sunday for business owners who suffered losses. "Those who break things will pay, repair the damage and be held accountable for their intention to sow chaos," Lescure said in a statement.

Bordeaux Mayor Thomas Cazenave said up to 100 stores had been looted in his city, while Marseille Mayor Benoit Payan announced emergency financial aid to support those businesses affected by the violence.   French retailer Carrefour's CEO Alexandre Bompard told French broadcaster BFMTV that 50 of the company's shops had been damaged, including 20 that were looted, with losses from the damage running into the tens of millions of euros.   The protests began last month over school conditions and teacher shortages in working-class suburbs, before broadening into a movement against inequality, public spending cuts and the rising cost of living.   More From This Section

item.title: Macron dénonce la "violence débridée" et appelle à la responsabilité
item.description: Emmanuel Macron a dénoncé une "violence débridée" qu'il a imputée à des "factieux" d'ultra-gauche et à des délinquants au lendemain des scènes de violence et de pillages qui ont terni une journée de vaste mobilisation contre la vie chère dans toute la France.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Emmanuel Macron a dénoncé une "violence débridée" qu'il a imputée à des "factieux" d'ultra-gauche et à des délinquants au lendemain des scènes de violence et de pillages qui ont terni une journée de vaste mobilisation contre la vie chère dans toute la France. Dans une allocution solennelle diffusée à la télévision au moment où Paris connaissait de nouvelles scènes de chaos, le chef de l'Etat a promis des aides rapides aux commerçants dont les magasins ont été pillés, affirmé que "ceux qui ont détruit doivent payer" et renvoyé sur les préfets et les maires la responsabilité d'interdire de futurs rassemblements. Appelant l'ensemble des partis politiques à faire preuve de responsabilité à sept mois de l'élection présidentielle, il a aussi promis de répondre aux "revendications légitimes" des manifestants, notamment celles des lycéens et des étudiants. Initialement né sur les réseaux sociaux, l'appel à manifester le 17 octobre avait été relayé par les syndicats lycéens qui se mobilisent depuis la mi-septembre pour obtenir de meilleures conditions d'enseignement, ainsi que par des organisations syndicales. Le ministère de l'Intérieur a dénombré 550.000 manifestants dans tout le pays, dont 110.000 à Paris, la CGT faisant état pour sa part de 800.000 personnes dans les cortèges, qui se sont dans l'ensemble déroulés sans incident. PRINCIPAUX DÉVELOPPEMENTS : 20h10 - Le président Emmanuel Macron dénonce la "violence débridée de factieux de la mouvance d'ultra-gauche et de délinquants", disant avoir éprouvé de la "honte" face à l'ampleur des dégradations. Dans une allocution solennelle, le chef de l'Etat a promis des aides aux commerçants victimes de pillages et renvoyé sur les préfets la responsabilité de "protéger nos villes, nos bâtiments publics et nos commerces", si besoin en interdisant certains rassemblements qui pourraient dégénérer. Prônant le dialogue avec les manifestants qui ont exprimé pacifiquement des revendications "légitimes", il a assuré que les autorités se montreraient "intraitables" avec les casseurs. "L'écoute et le dialogue ne signifient ni la faiblesse ni l'impunité", a-t-il dit. Emmanuel Macron a enfin demandé à l'ensemble des partis politiques et des syndicats de condamner les violences et d'appeler au calme pour permettre à la campagne de l'élection présidentielle de se dérouler dans les meilleures conditions. "Le pays a besoin d'ordre et d'apaisement", a-t-il plaidé. 18h20 - "La République, ce n'est pas le pillage", déclare Edouard Philippe, ancien Premier ministre d'Emmanuel Macron et candidat à l'élection présidentielle, en pointant du doigt la responsabilité de "l'ultra-gauche" dans les violences qui émaillent les mouvements sociaux. 18h00 - "Notre pays est pris en étau, voire en otage, entre la violence et l'impuissance", déclare Marine Le Pen dans une allocution aux Français. "Ce qui se joue aujourd'hui dépasse cette question de l'ordre public, nous vivons une crise profonde de confiance, d'autorité qui fait peser une menace sur la démocratie", ajoute la candidate du Rassemblement national en vue de la prochaine élection présidentielle. "Ces événements violents ne sont pas nés de rien, ils interviennent dans un contexte délétère que le gouvernement a lui même créé (...) Les inquiétudes, les souffrances, les plaintes des Français se sont transformées en exaspération et même parfois en colère. Ces colères sont souvent légitimes tant les crises se sont succédé sans qu'aucune décision ne soit prise, mais que les choses soient claires, très claires : il y a des millions de Français qui sont en colère mais qui ne cassent rien, qui ne pillent rien, ne brûlent rien. Je condamne ainsi fermement l'instrumentalisation de ces colères par des forces politiques qui encouragent la violence." 17h10 - "La France a été humiliée", déclare le président du Rassemblement national (RN), Jordan Bardella, à propos des violences qui ont émaillé la journée de samedi. "Que Macron s'en aille, demande pardon", ajoute le dirigeant d'extrême droite, dénonçant un dispositif de maintien de l'ordre "manifestement sous-dimensionné". 17h00 - De nouveaux heurts entre la police et des émeutiers ont lieu autour de la place de la République à Paris, montrent les images diffusées par les chaînes d'information en continu. 14h30 - Le ministre de l'Intérieur, Laurent Nuñez, annonce sur X un nouveau bilan de plus de 2.000 personnes interpellées et de plus de 600 policiers, gendarmes et pompiers blessés. 12h55 - Dans un communiqué, la Confédération des commerçants de France, qui dit représenter plus de 7.000 TPE du commerce et de l'artisanat dans les centre-villes, estime que près de 1.500 commerces ont été touchés à travers la France samedi. 12h45 - Emmanuel Macron réunira à 17h30 à l'Elysée le Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu et les ministres du gouvernement concernés et s'adressera solennellement aux Français à 20h00, annonce l'Elysée. 11h35 - "Je veux des explications et des moyens pour que cela ne se reproduise plus", déclare à la presse le maire socialiste de Marseille, Benoît Payan, alors que le ministre de l'Intérieur est attendu lundi dans la ville. "Mon propos n'est pas d'incriminer la police nationale. La police nationale, elle fait en fonction de qu'on lui demande (...). Je veux savoir quels ordres leurs ont été donnés, je veux savoir s'il leur a été demandé de s'occuper uniquement des manifestants et de lancer des lacrymos sur les manifestants et de ne pas s'occuper des pillages dans la ville." 11h20 - "Pendant une heure, je n'ai pas eu un seul policier national pour protéger la mairie", déclare sur BFM TV Guillaume Guérin, maire LR de Limoges. "On a un problème de soutien de nos forces de l'ordre", ajoute-t-il en déclarant avoir été informé par des policiers qu'ils manquaient de munitions. 11h00 - Le ministre de l'Intérieur, Laurent Nuñez, annonce sur X un bilan de 1.800 personnes interpellées samedi en France et de plus de 500 policiers, gendarmes et pompiers blessés. 10h45 - La secrétaire nationale des Ecologistes Marine Tondelier réclame sur X la démission du ministre de l'Intérieur Laurent Nuñez, "manifestement dépassé par la situation". 10h12 - "Ce bilan est désastreux car il emporte de lourdes conséquences : d’abord sur les libertés et notamment celle de manifester puisqu’elle est entravée par la violence ; ensuite sur la jeunesse confrontée à la brutalité et privée des réponses attendues du Gouvernement ; enfin sur l’État qui n’a pas été capable d’assurer partout l’ordre public", estime l'ancien président François Hollande dans un message sur X. 09h45 - A Lyon, le préfet du Rhône, Etienne Guyot, fait état de 160 personnes interpellées et placées en garde à vue et d'une centaine de membres des forces de l'ordre blessés. 08h50 - "Nous avons une ville dans une situation de délabrement total", déplore sur franceinfo la première adjointe au maire de Paris, Lamia El Araaje. "Nous avons assisté à des scènes de pillage méthodiques qui n'ont rien à voir avec les revendications sociales." "A l'évidence, les forces de l'ordre ont été débordées (...) Il y a eu clairement un manque de moyens", dit-elle. 08h15 - Une personne est décédée à la suite d'un arrêt cardiorespiratoire samedi à Paris lors des manifestations contre la vie chère, pendant lesquelles 855 interpellations ont été effectuées, ce qui représente un "chiffre record", déclare la préfecture de police dans un bilan établi à 08h00. Treize policiers et gendarmes et deux sapeurs-pompiers ont été blessés, ajoute-t-elle.

The spokesperson, briefing journalists after police spent the day searching the scene, said authorities had not yet found the vehicle and were still trying to determine whether the breach was an accident or a crime In August, investigators discovered [USN:L8N4420RI TEXT:"an explosive-laden drone"] near a runway at the airport, an event that German officials later said [USN:L8N44T1P2 TEXT:"Russia was responsible"] for. Russia has denied the allegations One runway had been closed but was again operating, the police spokesperson said German police first responded to the breach late on Saturday evening Leipzig police said they had not found suspicious objects or unauthorized people Officers on Sunday could be seen inspecting the area around a large break in the chain-link and barbed-wire fence

item.title: Rubio arrives in Central Asia while other US officials hit foreign policy hot spots
item.description: While the Iran war smolders, Saudi Arabia fights the Houthis and a new rift opens in US-Ukraine relations, Secretary of State Marco Rubio traveled on Sunday to Uzbekistan, a nation far removed from the biggest US foreign policy challenges.
item.dc:creator: Gram Slattery, Simon Lewis
item.content:encoded: While the Iran war smolders, Saudi Arabia fights the Houthis and a new rift opens in US-Ukraine relations, Secretary of State Marco Rubio traveled on Sunday to Uzbekistan, a nation far removed from the biggest US foreign policy challenges. The top US diplomat landed in Samarkand on Sunday night to meet with top officials from the C5+1, a grouping that brings together the United States and the Muslim-majority post-Soviet states of Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan. US officials have portrayed resource-rich Central Asia — the region between China, Russia and Iran — as worthy of more attention than it received from US President Donald Trump's predecessors. Trump hosted C5 leaders at the White House last November, when Kazakhstan agreed to join the Abraham Accords, a series of agreements under which Muslim-majority countries have normalized or deepened relations with Israel. Separately, Trump met with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev at the United Nations General Assembly in September of last year. Regional politics aside, the trip fits an emerging pattern in which Rubio often visits regions not at the center of the news cycle, while leaving some more fraught foreign policy portfolios to other Trump aides, including special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and Vice President JD Vance. Rubio has not visited Kyiv or Moscow since becoming secretary of state and was not present for talks between US and Ukrainian officials in Florida earlier this month, when US officials pressed Ukraine to stop hitting Russian refineries. Vance, not Rubio, represented the US in Pakistan during peace talks with Iran in April. Rubio's previous foreign trip, in early October, took him to Greece, Portugal and Iceland. Trump administration officials have typically rejected any suggestion that cabinet-level officials should focus their travels on geopolitical capitals and hot spots. Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau, for instance, said on X last week that the idea only certain destinations were worthy of visits from secretaries of state "perfectly encapsulates the decadence and degeneracy of the contemporary US foreign policy establishment." Speaking to reporters before leaving Washington on Saturday, Rubio said the timing of the Uzbekistan trip was dictated in part by the availability of the various delegations. He also said that foreign trips were too often designed to resolve immediate issues rather than build long-term relationships. "I mean, one of the things that suffers is the strategic business," Rubio told reporters. "You're always visiting someplace where there's a crisis or there's a problem or ... you're going because there's a conference." US-RUSSIA RELATIONS LOOM The delegation that greeted Rubio upon his arrival in Samarkand included Uzbek Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov, whom Rubio embraced warmly. Two women in traditional Uzbek attire presented Rubio and his wife with bouquets. One Central Asian diplomat, speaking on the condition of anonymity, said officials in the region were wondering to what extent the US would continue targeting Russian sanctions evasion. All C5 states, while drawing closer to the US, have deep historical ties with Moscow, and the region has facilitated Russian imports and exports that violate US and European Union sanctions, Western officials say. In the past, the US has pushed regional states to clamp down on those illicit flows. But Trump struck a deal with Moscow this month to [USN:L1N45Y0GJ TEXT:"import Russian diesel"], aimed at lowering domestic fuel prices before congressional midterm elections. On Friday, Trump [USN:L1N463009 TEXT:"waived"] all provisions of legislation that would have allowed him to slap massive tariffs on some nations that buy significant amounts of Russian crude oil or otherwise help Moscow evade sanctions. Among the nations that could have been affected, experts have said, are India and Kazakhstan. India, which Rubio will visit after Uzbekistan, remains the world's No. 2 Russian crude importer after China, despite Trump saying in February that India had agreed to stop buying oil from Russia. Additional questions hang over a potential trade deal with India and an expansion of the Abraham Accords in Central Asia. A US official, speaking on the condition of anonymity, described the trade deal on Friday as "pretty much done," raising the possibility that an agreement could be announced during the Rubio trip. Separately, the US [USN:L1N3TQ0WH TEXT:"has talked to"] additional Central Asian nations about joining the Abraham Accords, Reuters reported last year, conversations that potentially could continue in Samarkand. More than 200 business executives are accompanying Rubio to Uzbekistan, the State Department said. The Central Asian diplomat said the Trump administration has focused its commercial efforts on expanding access to the area's rare earth mineral resources. After Uzbekistan, Rubio will visit the Indian cities of Mumbai and Jamnagar to meet with business leaders, including Reliance Industries (RELI.NS) Chairman Mukesh Ambani, who earned the Trump administration's favor earlier in the year by backing a new refinery in Texas. Rubio most recently visited India five months ago. The trip is due to wrap up on Thursday.

item.title: ＭＬＢ＝リーグ優勝決定シリーズ、レイズが2勝2敗の五分に戻す
item.description: ［クリーブランド １７日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［クリーブランド　１７日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）は１７日、ア・リーグ優勝決定シリーズ（７回戦制）第４戦を行い、レイズがガーディアンズに７─３で勝利。対戦成績を２勝２敗の五分に戻した。

レイズは一回に１点を先制されたが、三回に２番ジョナサン・アランダ一塁手の適時打で追い付くと、六回に４番フニオール・カミネロ三塁手の適時二塁打で２─１と逆転。続く七回、アランダのタイムリーなどで３点を追加した。この後２点を失ったものの、九回に１番ヤンディ・ディアス指名打者の２ランで突き放した。

２０２３年から２５年までプロ野球巨人でプレーした、ガーディアンズのフォスター・グリフィン投手は二回から２番手として登板。３回２／３、４安打１失点の内容で勝敗は付かなかった。

シリーズ第５戦は１８日に行われる。

item.title: Rubio says Trump to take up to 60 days to weigh Russia sanctions
item.description: Ukraine's Zelenskiy says sanctions waiver will prolong war with Russia.
item.dc:creator: Nandita Bose, Gram Slattery
item.content:encoded: The day after waiving sanctions and tariffs related to Russian exports, US President Donald Trump said on Saturday he has yet to announce a final decision on the matter, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio said officials want more time to evaluate the situation. Rubio said on Saturday that the president will use up to 60 days to assess the economic impact of Russia-related sanctions and tariffs that he waived a day earlier. "A lot of you don't know what my decision is yet, but we'll figure it out, and you'll figure it out," Trump told reporters at his Mar-a-Lago club in Palm Beach, Florida. In a Truth Social post on Sunday, Trump wrote that his decision-making was aimed at avoiding anything "that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table." Trump signed an executive order on Friday waiving key sanctions and tariffs under the law known as the Graham Act, which he signed last month at the urging of lawmakers who want to pressure Moscow over its war in Ukraine. The measures, including tariffs on Russian goods and penalties on countries buying Russian oil and gas, were due to take effect next week. Friday's order did not specify how long the waiver would last, but Rubio said Trump opted for a 60-day review. "I think the president wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyze what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy and even to the US economy," Rubio told reporters before boarding a plane for a trip to Uzbekistan. Friday's executive order [USN:L1N463009 TEXT:"drew criticism"] from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, who warned it would embolden Russian President Vladimir Putin and prolong the war. DIESEL SUPPLIES Rubio on Saturday also defended a separate US agreement with Russia to increase diesel supplies to global markets, aimed at easing fuel prices that have climbed amid the war with Iran and disruptions to energy supplies. "That diesel is going to be sold one way or the other," Rubio said. "The only difference is how much of it the United States was going to get." Under the agreement, Trump said Russia initially would supply more than 300,000 metric tons of diesel to the United States, followed by shipments in November and beyond. The diesel agreement is "a carrot to try to end the war, not an economic lifeline" to Russia, US Secretary of Energy Chris Wright said during a Sunday interview on ABC's "This Week." But "the only way they can get additional diesel to export is if they turn down the conflict with Ukraine," Wright told CNN's "State of the Union" program on Sunday. “If Russia can bring additional diesel to the market and export it, it would benefit American consumers,” he told CNN. “He's putting pressure that would both benefit American consumers and be a step forward for peace in the Russia-Ukraine war.” Rubio said the diesel deal and sanctions waiver reflected the challenge of managing conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine that have disrupted global energy supplies. "These conflicts around the world are starting to crash into each other," he said.

item.title: サッカー＝インテルがボローニャに逆転勝ち、開幕から無敗キープ
item.description: ［１７日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１７日　ロイター］ - サッカーのイタリア・セリエＡは１７日、各地で試合を行い、インテルがボローニャに３─１で逆転勝利を収め、開幕からの無敗をキープした。

インテルは前半１０分に失点するも、同４４分にマルクス・テュラムのゴールで追い付くと、後半２４分にカルロス・アウグストが決めて逆転に成功。同３８分にも１点を加えた。

その他、ローマはジェノアに２─０で勝利し、ナポリはベネチアに０─１で敗れた。

インテルは７試合を終えて６勝１分けで勝ち点１９。２位ローマとの同２差をキープしている。

item.title: Saudi-led coalition says helicopter crash in Najran kills two crew members
item.description: A reconnaissance AH-6i helicopter crashed in the Najran region of Saudi Arabia, killing its two crew members, the Saudi-led coalition's spokesperson Major General Turki al-Maliki said in a statement on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A reconnaissance AH-6i helicopter crashed in the Najran region of Saudi Arabia, killing its two crew members, the Saudi-led coalition's spokesperson Major General Turki al-Maliki said in a statement on Sunday. The helicopter crashed due to a technical malfunction in an area under the jurisdiction of the Saudi National Guard Ministry, the statement added. Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis released footage later on Sunday of what they said was a Saudi AH-6i helicopter being shot down by a missile while carrying out what they described as hostile activities near Najran. The footage did not clearly show the incident, and Reuters could not immediately verify the Houthis' claim. There was no immediate comment from Saudi authorities. On Saturday, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said on X that the group had shot down a Saudi Apache helicopter near Najran. It was not clear if that referred to the same incident. Al-Maliki commented on Saree's post on Sunday with a photo of several Apaches lined up, saying: "You claim to have shot it down, but it will enter the battlefield soon." Separately, the Saudi civil defence said on Sunday that six people were injured after a projectile it said was fired by Houthis fell on a residential area in Najran. Najran has been hit by attacks from the Houthis in recent weeks as fighting between the coalition and the Yemen-based group escalated, with the [USN:L1N4620VJ TEXT:"Yemen conflict"] becoming another front in the US-led war with Iran .

item.title: テニス＝マスターズ上海大会、第1シードのズベレフ準決勝敗退
item.description: ［上海（中国） １７日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［上海（中国）　１７日　ロイター］ - 男子テニスのマスターズ上海大会は１７日、シングルス準決勝を行い、第１シードのアレクサンダー・ズベレフ（ドイツ）は敗退した。

今季を世界ランキング１位で終えることが確定しているズベレフは第２５シードのアレハンドロ・ダビドビッチ・フォキナ（スペイン）に７─５、４─６、３─６で逆転負け。３６本のウィナーを打たれて２時間２分で屈し、同選手との８回目の直接対決で２敗目を喫した。

ダビドビッチ・フォキナはマスターズ１０００では準優勝に終わった２０２２年のマスターズ・モンテカルロ大会以来となる、通算２回目の決勝進出を達成した。

準決勝のもう１試合では、第１２シードのラファエル・ホダル（スペイン）がロシア出身で第５シードの元世界ランク１位、ダニル・メドベージェフに６─３、６─４で勝利。大会史上最年少、２０歳で決勝進出を果たした。同選手がマスターズ１０００の決勝に進んだのはこれが初めて。

item.title: サッカー＝バルセロナ5得点で圧勝、開幕から9戦全勝
item.description: ［セビリア（スペイン） １７日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［セビリア（スペイン）　１７日　ロイター］ - サッカーのスペイン１部は１７日、各地で試合を行い、首位バルセロナがベティスを５─２で下し、開幕９戦全勝とした。

バルセロナは前半１０分、右サイドで仕掛けたラミン・ヤマルがペナルティーエリア右端から左足で先制。２─１で迎えた後半６分にはヤマルのお膳立てからガブリエル・ジェズスが決めてリードを広げた。

対するベティスは同８分にエズ・アブデのゴールで１点差に詰め寄るも、その直後の小競り合いでファクンド・ベルナルがヤマルに頭突きを見舞ったとして退場処分となり、１０人での戦いを強いられた。バルセロナはその後、ヤマルのＦＫのこぼれ球をエリック・ガルシアが決めると、最後はダニ・オルモが締めくくった。

佐藤龍之介が所属するバレンシアは、ビルバオとスコアレスドロー。佐藤はベンチ入りしたが出場はなかった。

その他、アトレチコ・マドリードはエスパニョールに１─０で勝利。ビリャレアルとエルチェはスコアレスドローに終わった。

９試合を終えて、バルセロナは勝ち点２７とし、２位アトレチコとの５ポイント差をキープ。ここまで計３９得点と圧倒的な強さを示している。

item.title: フランスの大規模抗議デモが一部暴徒化、近年最悪の暴動に 生活費高騰に不満
item.description:
Janis Laizans Stamos Prousalis Yann Tessier
[パリ １７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Janis Laizans　Stamos Prousalis 　Yann Tessier

[パリ １７日 ロイター] - フランス各地で１７日、生活費の高騰と公共サービスの質の低下に抗議するデモが一部で暴徒化し、同国で過去数十年で最大規模の暴動に発展した。

生活費の上昇を背景に、ベルギー、ポルトガル、イタリアでも同日、抗議デモが行われた。アルバニアでは、政府の腐敗への不満や雇用不足、教育水準の低さに抗議する人々が再び集まった。

フランスでは数十都市で数十万人が平和的に街頭行進する一方、一部の過激なグループが公共施設を標的にし、高級ブティックやスーパーマーケットを略奪し、警察車両や警官を襲撃した。

中部リモージュでは市庁舎が放火され、マルセイユでは黒ずくめのデモ参加者が市庁舎に乱入して無政府主義的な落書きをし、リヨンでは市の観光案内所が放火された。

ルコルニュ仏首相は、政府は暴力に「屈しない」と表明。騒乱は「極左」と犯罪者によるものだと非難した。

フランスでは２０２７年に大統領選が行われる予定で、同氏はＸに「この暴力を大統領選前の予行演習として利用しようとしている者たちに、はっきり言う。われわれは屈しない。誰であれ、暴力によって政治的な要求を押し付けることはできない」と投稿した。

同氏は夕方に現場を視察した際、抗議行動に関連して約１２００人を拘束したと述べた。

ヌニェス内相によると、全国のデモ参加者は約５５万人。仏労働総同盟（ＣＧＴ）はロイターに対し、参加者は８０万人と推計していると述べた。

マクロン大統領は、襲撃を実行した者を訴追し、処罰すると表明した。同氏はＸに「われわれの制度を損ない、平和的に要求を訴える人々を妨害することだけを狙う、混乱を引き起こす者たちに対し、われわれは一致団結して立ち向かう」と投稿した。

パリのデモ参加者、ローラさん（１９）は「私たちが声を上げているのは、生活費の負担があまりに重く、燃料価格が高すぎるからだ。高校生たちは、教員の増員やまともな学習環境を求めて抗議しているだけなのに、全国で暴力的な攻撃を受け、けがをしている」と語った。

＜催涙ガス、放火、略奪も＞

大半の抗議行動は正午ごろに始まったが、デモの正式な開始時刻より前に始まったものもあった。

パリの一部地区では、警察が若者を中心とするデモ参加者に押されて後退しながら催涙弾を発射した。参加者の多くは黒い服を着て、催涙ガスに備えてフードやマスク、ゴーグルを着用していた。暴徒たちは中心部の百貨店「ギャラリー・ラファイエット」への侵入を試み、銀行や店舗を荒らし、携帯電話会社の店舗を襲撃した。デモ参加者による放火は終日続き、多数の車などが燃やされた。

ベルギーのブリュッセルでは、フランスの抗議行動に触発されたとみられる若者ら数百人がデモを行い、一部が警察と衝突した。ベルギーの学生団体は、教育費の上昇と、高等教育を受けにくくする恐れがある改革に抗議していると説明している。

アルバニアでは、ラマ首相の辞任を求める学生の大規模デモが５日目に入り、警察が参加者に向けてゴム弾とみられる弾丸を発射した。

住宅費やその他の生活費への抗議行動が数日間続いているポルトガルでは、数万人がリスボンの街頭に繰り出した。ポルトガルの住宅価格は２０１７年以来２倍に跳ね上がり、住宅取得の困難さは欧州でも最も深刻な水準にある。

イタリアでは、ミラノで生活費の高騰に抗議するデモ行進が混乱に陥り、警察は催涙ガスを使用して中心部の大聖堂広場を制圧した。ＡＮＳＡ通信によると、ボローニャでは別の抗議デモが暴徒化し、警察が群衆を解散させるために放水車を使用。７人を拘束した。

＜仏警察の対応に批判＞

フランスの抗議行動は９月、労働者層が多いパリ北部郊外の高校で始まった。教員不足や施設の老朽化に対する怒りが、格差や公共支出、生活水準を巡る幅広い抗議運動に発展した。

パリでは１７日、蛍光ベストを着た抗議者たちが道路を封鎖した。フランスでは、マクロン大統領の一期目も「黄色いベスト運動」と呼ばれる抗議活動が起きたが、今回のデモ参加者数は当時のピーク時の規模を上回った。ただ、２３年の年金制度改革反対デモの規模には及ばなかった。

デモ参加者に負傷者が出たことを受け、警察の対応に批判が集まっている。警察の監察機関は、警察による暴力行為の疑いがある少なくとも２４件について調査を始めた。

ルコルニュ首相は、１７日の抗議活動で１５０人以上の警察官が負傷したと述べたが、デモ参加者に負傷者がいたかどうかについては言及しなかった。

ヌニェス内相は、１７日の警察との衝突で１人が片手を失ったとの報道を確認した。フランスのメディアによると、この人物は閃光手りゅう弾を拾おうとしたとされる。

警察労組ＵＮＳＡは、複数の場所で群衆がこん棒やれんがを使って警察車両を襲う映像をＸに投稿した。同労組は政府に対し、警察は限界に達しつつあると警告した。

item.title: Deaths confirmed after 'serious incident,' fire at Canada military base in Alberta
item.description: People were killed and injured in a serious incident that resulted in a fire on one of Canada's busiest military bases in Alberta, Defense Minister David McGuinty said on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Amanda Stephenson
item.content:encoded: People were killed and injured in a serious incident that resulted in a fire on one of Canada's busiest military bases in Alberta, Defense Minister David McGuinty said on Saturday. "I'm saddened to share that there have been both fatalities and injuries as a result of an incident" at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, McGuinty told reporters in Ottawa. He did not say how many people were killed or injured, or what caused the "tragic" situation at the base in the east-central part of the province, about 210 km (130 miles) east of Edmonton. A major fire was still burning on Saturday evening, he said, adding: "I cannot recall an incident like this in recent memory." The Canadian military and the Royal Canadian Mounted Police are investigating the incident, McGuinty said. Prime Minister Mark Carney posted on social media that the national government was "working closely with the Government of Alberta and local authorities." CFB Wainwright had 1,310 military and civilian personnel stationed there as of 2021, according to census data. The town of Wainwright, population about 6,600, is just north of the base. The municipality posted on social media that the fire had crossed the base fence into the nearby district but no evacuation orders had been issued. General Jennie Carignan, the chief of Canada's Defense Staff, said on social media that the Canadian forces are fully engaged with federal, provincial and local authorities. "Our priority remains the welfare of our members, their families and their community," she said. (This story has been corrected to add the dropped word 'not' in paragraph 3.)

item.title: ＮＢＡ＝ドラフト全体1位指名、ウィザーズのディバンツァが負傷
item.description: ［１７日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１７日　ロイター］　 - 米プロバスケットボール協会（ＮＢＡ）ウィザーズは、今年のドラフトの全体１位で指名したフォワードのＡＪ・ディバンツァ（１９）が、１６日に行われたプレシーズン最終戦のペリカンズ戦で足首に軽度の捻挫を負ったと発表した。

ディバンツァはこの試合の第２クオーターにジャンプシュートを放った後、ぎこちない形で着地し、転倒。足を引きずりながらロッカールームへと下がった。約１５分プレーし、１２得点を挙げたが、ウィザーズは１０６─１０７で負けた。

ブライアン・キーフ・ヘッドコーチはディバンツァについて、大事を取って交代させたとコメント。同選手はさらに検査を受ける予定という。同選手はブリガムヤング大学で１年プレーし、全米トップの１試合平均２５．５得点をマークした。

ウィザーズは２１日に地元で行われるシーズン開幕戦でバックスと対戦する。

item.title: サッカー＝チェルシーＧＫマルティネス、脳震とうで病院に搬送
item.description: ［リバプール １７日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［リバプール　１７日　ロイター］ - サッカーのイングランド・プレミアリーグ、チェルシーのＧＫエミリアノ・マルティネス（３４）は１７日、エバートン戦で相手選手と衝突して脳震とうを起こし、病院に搬送された。

マルティネスはゴール前でＦＫに対応しようとした際、エバートンのジャラッド・ブランスウェイトと激突。ブランスウェイトは治療を受けた後に立ち上がったが、マルティネスは地面に横たわったまま治療を受けたのち、担架でピッチから運び出された。

チェルシーのシャビアロンソ監督は「脳震とうということ以外は分からない」とした上で、「彼は搬送されたとき意識はあり、今は病院で念のため検査を受けている。重傷ではないことを願っているが、待つしかない」と述べた。

後半３０分からマルティネスに代わり、２１歳のＧＫマイク・ペンダースが出場。プレミアリーグデビューを果たし、チームにとってリーグ戦では１月以来となる完封に貢献した。チェルシーはペドロ・ネトが２ゴールを挙げ、２─０で勝利した。

item.title: サッカー＝イプスウィッチ前田、マンＣ戦でプレミア初ゴール
item.description: ［ロンドン １７日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ロンドン　１７日　ロイター］ - サッカーのイングランド・プレミアリーグは１７日、各地で試合を行い、イプスウィッチの前田大然がマンチェスター・シティー（マンＣ）戦で同リーグでの初ゴールを挙げた。

先発した前田は先制された２分後の前半２１分、右サイドで味方からのパスに追い付き、左足でシュート。開幕から７試合目で待望の初得点をマークした。この後アーリング・ハーランドに２ゴールを決められたイプスウィッチは、後半４５分にＰＫで１点を返したが、２─３で敗戦。前田は後半２６分までプレーした。

ＧＫ鈴木彩艶が所属するアストンビラはニューカッスルに１─０で勝利。鈴木はフル出場を果たし、今季初の完封勝利に貢献した。リバプールはブレントフォードに２─１で逆転勝ち。リバプールの遠藤航はベンチ入りしたが、出場しなかった。

守田英正が所属するハルはフラムに０─１で敗戦。守田は後半３０分から出場した。チェルシーはエバートンに２─０で快勝した。

開幕７連勝のマンＣが勝ち点２１で首位。チェルシーが同１３の４位、リバプールが同１２の暫定５位に浮上した。ハルは９位でイプスウィッチは１０位。今季２勝目を挙げたアストンビラは暫定１２位に上がった。

item.title: サッカー＝バイエルン6ゴール圧勝で暫定首位浮上、伊藤は出番なし
item.description: ［ミュンヘン（ドイツ） １７日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ミュンヘン（ドイツ）　１７日　ロイター］　 - サッカーのドイツ１部ブンデスリーガは１７日、各地で試合を行い、伊藤洋輝が所属するバイエルン・ミュンヘンがライプチヒを６─１で下し、暫定首位に浮上した。

ホームのバイエルンは前半１２分にルイス・ディアスのゴールで先制すると、前半のうちに３─０とリードを広げ、後半にも立ち上がりの２分にディアスが加点。同８分には、これがブンデスリーガ通算１００試合目の出場となったハリー・ケーンがゴールを挙げ、最後はディアスがハットトリックを達成した。失点は同アディショナルタイムに喫した１点のみだった。

伊藤はこの試合でベンチ入りしたが、最後まで出番はなかった。

佐野海舟がフル出場したマインツは、田中聡フル出場のシャルケに１─０で勝利。マインツの川崎颯太はベンチ入りしなかった。

ドルトムントがウニオン・ベルリンと０─０のドローに終わったため、６試合消化段階でバイエルンが勝ち点１４でドルトムントと並び、得失点差により暫定首位に浮上した。

item.title: ボクシング＝亀田和毅のタイトルマッチ、相手の体調不良で当日中止に
item.description: ［１７日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１７日　ロイター］ - プロボクシングの亀田和毅（３５）は１７日、米ラスベガスで世界ボクシング協会（ＷＢＡ）世界フェザー級タイトルマッチを行う予定だったが、対戦相手の体調不良により、試合当日に中止となった。米ボクシング専門サイト、ボクシングシーンなどが報じている。

ブランドン・フィゲロア（２９、米国）は１６日の前日計量で規定体重（５７．１５キロ）を２回クリアできず、体重超過でタイトルを剥奪されていた。１回目の計量では約０．６キロのオーバー。１時間後に行われた２回目の計量でも体重は減っていなかった。

亀田はこの試合に勝てば新王者となり、引き分けか負けた場合、王座は空位となる予定だった。亀田の戦績は４２勝５敗。フィゲロアは２６勝２敗１分け。

item.title: ゴルフ＝竹田は首位と5打差の4位、ビュイックＬＰＧＡ
item.description: ［１７日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１７日　ロイター］　 - 米女子ゴルフのビュイックＬＰＧＡは１７日、中国・上海の佘山国際ＧＣ（パー７２）で第３ラウンドを行い、竹田麗央は前日の４位をキープした。

竹田は４バーディー、１ダブルボギー、１ボギーの１アンダー７１で回り、通算４アンダーの２１２。ＬＰＧＡツアー初優勝を目指す、首位チェ・ヘジン（韓国）とは５打差となった。

４０位でスタートした吉田優利は６バーディー、１ボギーの５アンダー６７をマーク。通算イーブンパーの９位で、ディフェンディングチャンピオンのジーノ・ティティクル（タイ）らと並んだ。

４位で出た原英莉花は７６とスコアを崩し、通算１オーバーの１４位に後退。勝みなみは通算７オーバーの４０位、西郷真央は通算８オーバーの４６位となった。

item.title: US wants Israel to 'crack down' on settler violence in West Bank, Rubio says
item.description: "We're very disturbed by those images and what we're seeing," Marco Rubio said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The United States wants Israel to do more to deter attacks committed by settlers in the West Bank, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday. "We're very disturbed by those images and what we're seeing," Rubio said. "We've asked the Israelis and continue to ask them to crack down on that stuff." His comments to reporters came after the widespread dissemination of video showing multiple individuals attacking Heidi Levine, an American photojournalist with the Washington Post. Levine was one of at least two people injured in the Friday incident, which took place as Israeli settlers [USN:L6N46304S TEXT:"attacked"] Palestinian civilians. European diplomats and a French mayor also were attacked in the occupied West Bank, Belgium's foreign minister said. The US State Department, Rubio said, has inquired about the event that included Levine's attack. Rubio, who spoke to reporters before boarding a flight to Uzbekistan, said he expects to hear back from the US Embassy in Jerusalem by Sunday. Israeli settlers in the West Bank have been involved in at least 170 attacks on Palestinians since September 27, around the start of the annual olive harvest, according to Yesh Din, an Israeli settlements monitoring group.

item.title: Kenya confirms four new Ebola cases, bringing total number to seven
item.description: The cases are the first known infections passed on inside Kenya, where the first patient arrived from Congo on Oct 3.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

Kenya confirms four new Ebola cases, bringing total number to seven

The cases are the first known infections passed on inside Kenya, where the first patient arrived from Congo on Oct 3.

A tent which has been erected to screen travellers within the health port services at the Malaba crossing-point between Kenya and Uganda after a man who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled and died of a new Ebola outbreak involving the Bundibugyo species at the Nairobi Hospital, in Malaba, Kenya Oct 8, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Jackson Adika)

18 Oct 2026 04:52AM

FAST

Kenya confirmed four new cases of the Ebola Bundibugyo virus on Saturday (Oct 17), including three health workers who treated the country's first patient, bringing the total number of confirmed cases to seven, the health ministry said. The other new case is a male relative of the index patient, who died. The relative had been in quarantine since Oct 6, the ministry said in a statement. The cases are the first known infections passed on inside Kenya, where the first patient arrived from Congo on Oct 3. But the ministry says it has traced and quarantined nearly all of his contacts and there is no evidence that the virus is spreading in the community . The three health workers, two men and a woman aged 29, 35 and 32 respectively, managed the index case on Oct 3 and 4 and had been in quarantine since Oct 9, it said. All four new patients were already in quarantine when they developed symptoms and were diagnosed.

The second and third patients confirmed earlier are stable and responding well to supportive treatment, the ministry said. It said 128 of 130 listed contacts, or 98.5 percent, had been traced and placed in quarantine, higher than the 85 percent global benchmark it said was needed to break the chain of transmission. Kenya's cases are linked to the Ebola epidemic in Congo, the second-largest outbreak ever recorded, with more than 9,000 cases and more than 4,000 deaths.

Related:

Tan Kiat How on low risk of Ebola cross-border transmission to Singapore

WHO says Congo Ebola outbreak can still be brought under control within three months

Commentary: This Ebola outbreak should never have caught the world off guard

There are no approved vaccines or treatments for the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola. The first Kenyan case was a man who had been ill in Congo for about a month before travelling by road to Uganda and flying to Nairobi on Oct 3. He died on Oct 5. His arrival has raised concerns about screening at the Congo-Uganda border, which has been closed since May, and at Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International Airport. Efforts to trace the remaining two contacts were ongoing, the ministry said. "The risk to the general public remains low as there is no evidence of community transmission," it said, adding that there were no restrictions on travel, trade or public gatherings.

Source: Reuters/fs

item.description: ローマ教皇が退院、肺腺がん手術後の検査良好 日曜の祈りに参加へ Reuters

item.title: ローマ教皇が退院、肺腺がん手術後の検査良好 日曜の祈りに参加へ
item.description:
Joshua McElwee
[バチカン市 １７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Joshua McElwee

[バチカン市 １７日 ロイター] - 肺腺がんの手術を受けたローマ教皇レオ１４世が１７日、入院していたローマの病院を退院した。教皇庁（バチカン）によると、１８日の日曜の祈りに参加する予定という。

教皇はローマのジェメリ病院の外で手を振って見送りの人々に応えながら、自力で歩いて待機していた車に向かった。

教皇は１３日に、がん組織を全て除去するため右肺の下葉を切除する手術を受けた。手術後の経過は良好で１６日にはロシアのプーチン大統領と電話会談していた。

医師団は１７日、血液検査や胸部画像検査を行った結果、教皇は退院できる状態にあり、日常の活動も自立して行うことができると述べた。

教皇は１１月６─１７日にウルグアイ、アルゼンチン、ペルーを訪問する予定。

item.title: Mass protests in France spiral into worst riots in years
item.description: French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu blamed the unrest on the "ultra-left" and criminals.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

Mass protests in France spiral into worst riots in years

French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu blamed the unrest on the "ultra-left" and criminals.

French riot police run amid clashes with protesters in Paris as protests take place across France on Oct 17, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Abdul Saboor)

18 Oct 2026 02:03AM (Updated: 18 Oct 2026 03:06PM)

FAST

PARIS: Rioting erupted in cities across France on Saturday (Oct 17) as demonstrations against rising living costs and declining public services spiralled out of control in some of the worst violence the country has witnessed for decades. While hundreds of thousands protested peacefully in street marches in scores of cities, violent fringe groups targeted public buildings, looted luxury boutiques and supermarkets and attacked police vehicles and officers. In Limoges, the city hall was set ablaze; in Marseille, black-clad protesters broke into city hall and defaced the building with anarchic graffiti, and in Lyon, protesters torched the city's tourist office. French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said the government would not be "intimidated" by violence, and blamed the unrest on the "ultra-left" and criminals just months before a presidential election next year.

"To those who clearly want to use this violence as a 'warm-up' before the presidential election, I say clearly: We will not let ourselves be intimidated. No one will impose their political agenda through violence," he wrote in a post on X. About 1,200 people had been arrested as part of the protests, Lecornu added while visiting the sites in the evening. Around 550,000 people had participated in the demonstrations across the country, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said. The CGT union told Reuters it estimated protesters at 800,000 people.

Related:

Teenager shoots headmaster, teacher at French school

France students plan more protests, UN 'concerned' over violence

France pledges more teachers after school students vow no let-up

President Emmanuel Macron vowed to prosecute and punish people who had carried out the attacks. "We will all stand united against the sowers of chaos, who only seek to undermine our institutions and prevent those who peacefully express their demands from doing so," he wrote in a post on X. Belgium, Portugal and Italy also faced smaller-scale protests on Saturday as living costs rise in Europe, while protesters in Albania again rallied against perceived government corruption, a lack of jobs and poor education standards. Protesters said most people had marched peacefully, and put much of the violence down to troublemakers who had set out to cause damage and clash with the police. Many held signs bearing slogans against the police, the president and the wealthy. "We are fighting because the cost of living is too harsh, because the price of fuel is too high, because high school pupils are being violently attacked and hurt all over the country just for trying to protest and ask for more teachers and decent learning conditions," said Lola, a 19-year-old protester in Paris.

A Centaure, a multi-purpose intervention armoured vehicle of the French Gendarmerie Nationale, is seen in a street amid clashes between protesters and the French riot police as protests take place across France on Oct 17, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Manon Cruz)

TEAR GAS, FIRE AND LOOTING Most protests kicked off around midday, with some beginning before the official start of the demonstrations. In some parts of Paris, police fired tear gas rounds as they retreated in the face of mostly young protesters, many of whom were dressed in black and wore hoodies, masks and goggles to protect against tear gas. Rioters tried to break into the Galeries Lafayette department store, smashed up banks, ransacked a Lacoste store as well as other boutiques and looted an SFR mobile phone shop. Protesters had been setting objects ablaze all day, including numerous cars. In protests partly inspired by those in France, several hundred mostly young people protested in Brussels, and some clashed with police. Belgian student groups have said they are protesting against rising education costs and reforms they fear will make higher education less accessible. In Albania, police fired what appeared to be rubber bullets at protesters during a fifth day of mass student demonstrations calling for Prime Minister Edi Rama to step down. In Portugal, tens of thousands took to the streets of Lisbon following days of unrest to protest against housing and other living costs. Housing prices in Portugal have doubled since 2017, fuelling one of the worst affordability crises in Europe. In Italy, a march against high costs of living in Milan degenerated into disorder, with police clearing the central cathedral square with tear gas. Police in Bologna used water cannons to try to disperse crowds and made seven arrests after another protest turned violent, the ANSA news agency reported.

FRENCH POLICE RESPONSE UNDER SCRUTINY The protests in France began last month at high schools in Paris' working-class northern suburbs, where anger over teacher shortages and shabby facilities evolved into a broader movement focused on inequality, public spending and living standards. In Paris on Saturday, protesters in high-visibility vests blocked streets, recalling the Yellow Vest movement that marked Macron's previous term in office. Saturday's protests eclipsed the size of the crowds at the peak of the Yellow Vest movement, though they were far lower than the levels seen at the protests in 2023 against Macron's pension overhaul. Macron is entering the final stretch of his presidency, facing a fragmented political landscape and growing pressure over the economy. France's efforts to reduce public debt have not reassured investors, pushing government borrowing costs to their highest levels in over two decades. Police tactics have drawn criticism following injuries among demonstrators, including a teenager who lost a hand. The police watchdog is investigating at least two dozen allegations of police violence. Lecornu said more than 150 police officers had been injured in Saturday's protests, but did not say whether any protesters had been hurt. Nunez confirmed reports that one person had his hand torn off in clashes with police on Saturday. French media reported he tried to pick up a stun grenade. The UNSA police union posted a video on X showing crowds attacking police vans with clubs and bricks in multiple locations. The union warned the government police forces were at breaking point. "Today again, in every corner of France, our colleagues are being used as punching bags. Pelted with stones, injured, trapped in real ambushes," the union said. "Let everyone take responsibility: this cannot go on indefinitely. The rope is stretched to its maximum."

Source: Reuters/fs/kg
